explanation: January 12 was proclaimed National Youth Day (Rashtriya Yuva Diwas) in 1984 by the Government of India to inspire youth with the philosophies, ideals, and teachings of Swami Vivekananda.

title: National Science Day is celebrated across India on February 28 every year to honor the discovery of which landmark scientific breakthrough?
subject: General Awareness & Logic

options.text: The Raman Effect by Sir C. V. Raman in 1928
The formulation of Saha Ionization Equation
The first successful atomic test at Pokhran

explanation: On February 28, 1928, Sir Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman announced the discovery of the Raman Effect (inelastic light scattering), for which he received the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics.

title: Good Governance Day is observed in India on December 25 every year to mark the birth anniversary of which former Prime Minister of India?
subject: General Awareness & Logic
explanation: Established in 2014, Good Governance Day (Sushasan Divas) honors Bharat Ratna Atal Bihari Vajpayee, fostering awareness of accountable, transparent, and responsive public administration.

title: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas (Non-Resident Indian Day) is celebrated on January 9 every two years to commemorate which historic return to India?
subject: General Awareness & Logic

options.text: Mahatma Gandhi's return from South Africa in 1915
Subhas Chandra Bose's arrival in Singapore in 1943
Rabindranath Tagore's Nobel tour return in 1913
Swami Vivekananda's return from Chicago Parliament in 1897

explanation: On January 9, 1915, Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa, leading the struggle for freedom. Pravasi Bharatiya Divas honors the vital contributions of the overseas Indian diaspora.

title: Earth Day is celebrated internationally on April 22 every year. What was the global campaign theme for Earth Day 2024?
subject: General Awareness & Logic

options.text: 'Planet vs. Plastics' (advocating a 60% reduction in plastics by 2040)

explanation: Earth Day 2024 rallied under the theme 'Planet vs. Plastics', demanding a 60% reduction in the production of all plastics by 2040 and an end to single-use plastics to protect human and planetary health.

title: National Sports Day (Rashtriya Khel Divas) is observed across India on August 29 every year to mark the birth anniversary of which sports icon?
subject: General Awareness & Logic

options.text: Major Dhyan Chand ('The Wizard of Hockey')

explanation: Major Dhyan Chand led India to three Olympic Gold medals in field hockey (1928 Amsterdam, 1932 Los Angeles, 1936 Berlin). His birth anniversary is marked by the presentation of national sports awards by the President of India.

title: Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) is celebrated in India on November 26 every year to commemorate:
subject: General Awareness & Logic

options.text: The formal adoption of the Constitution by the Constituent Assembly in 1949
The commencement of the Constitution as a Republic in 1950
The first meeting of the Drafting Committee under Dr. Ambedkar
The signing of the Objectives Resolution by Jawaharlal Nehru

explanation: On November 26, 1949, the Constituent Assembly of India formally adopted the Constitution of India, which subsequently came into full effect on January 26, 1950 (Republic Day).

title: World Health Day is observed globally on April 7 each year to mark the founding anniversary of which United Nations agency in 1948?
subject: General Awareness & Logic
explanation: World Health Day marks the founding of the WHO in 1948. The theme for World Health Day 2024 was 'My Health, My Right', championing universal access to quality healthcare, education, clean water, and nutrition.

title: National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas) is celebrated in India on October 31 every year to commemorate the birth anniversary of:
subject: General Awareness & Logic

options.text: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel ('The Iron Man of India')

explanation: Introduced in 2014, National Unity Day pays tribute to Sardar Patel's monumental leadership in integrating 565 princely states into the Indian Union, celebrated with the nationwide 'Run for Unity'.

title: World Wildlife Day is celebrated on March 3 each year to celebrate and raise awareness of the world's wild animals and plants, marking the signature of which 1973 international convention?
subject: General Awareness & Logic

options.text: CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species)

explanation: March 3 commemorates the adoption of CITES in Washington D.C. in 1973. The 2024 World Wildlife Day theme was 'Connecting People and Planet: Exploring Digital Innovation in Wildlife Conservation'.

title: Proclaimed by UNESCO in 1999, International Mother Language Day is observed worldwide on February 21 each year, tracing its origins to the 1952 Language Movement in:
subject: General Awareness & Logic

options.text: Canada (defending French language rights in Quebec)

explanation: On February 21, 1952, students in Dhaka were killed while protesting for the official recognition of their mother language, Bengali. UNESCO established the day to promote linguistic diversity and multilingual education.

title: World Water Day is celebrated globally on March 22 each year under the auspices of UN-Water. What was the official theme for World Water Day 2024?
subject: General Awareness & Logic
explanation: World Water Day 2024 highlighted 'Water for Peace', underscoring that water can create peace or spark conflict when scarce or contaminated, urging cross-border cooperation on shared transboundary river basins.

title: The United Nations General Assembly declared the period 2021 to 2030 as the UN Decade on:
subject: General Awareness & Logic
explanation: Led by UNEP and FAO, the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration (2021-2030) is a rallying call for the protection and revival of ecosystems across continents and oceans to counter climate change and halt biodiversity loss.

title: Which law of thermodynamics defines the concept of temperature by stating that if two systems are each in thermal equilibrium with a third system, they are in thermal equilibrium with each other?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The Zeroth Law establishes thermal equilibrium as an equivalence relation, enabling the construction and calibration of thermometers.

title: According to the First Law of Thermodynamics (ΔU = Q - W), in an adiabatic process where no heat enters or leaves the system (Q = 0), the change in internal energy is equal to:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: The negative of the work done by the system (-W)
The total enthalpy change of the surroundings

explanation: In an adiabatic process Q = 0, so ΔU = -W. If the system expands and does work on the surroundings, its internal energy and temperature decrease.

title: What is the maximum theoretical efficiency of a Carnot heat engine operating between a hot reservoir at 600 K and a cold reservoir at 300 K?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Carnot efficiency η = 1 - (T_cold / T_hot) = 1 - (300 / 600) = 0.50 or 50%.

title: Which fundamental thermodynamic quantity is defined as a measure of molecular disorder or the number of microscopic configurations corresponding to a macroscopic state?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Entropy is a measure of molecular randomness and the dispersal of energy, defined statistically by Boltzmann as S = k * ln(W).

title: The Third Law of Thermodynamics states that the entropy of a perfect, pure crystalline substance at absolute zero temperature (0 Kelvin) is:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Equal to the gas constant R

explanation: At absolute zero (0 K), thermal motion ceases and a perfect crystal has only one unique ground state microstate (W = 1), so S = k * ln(1) = 0.

title: In an isothermal expansion of an ideal gas at constant temperature T, which thermodynamic property of the gas remains completely unchanged?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: For an ideal gas, internal energy depends solely on temperature (U = nCvT). In an isothermal process ΔT = 0, so ΔU = 0.

title: An isobaric thermodynamic process is characterized by which state variable being held strictly constant throughout the transformation?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: An isobaric process occurs at constant pressure (ΔP = 0). The work done during an isobaric expansion is W = P * ΔV.

title: An isochoric (or isometric) thermodynamic process is one in which which quantity remains strictly constant?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: In an isochoric process ΔV = 0, meaning no boundary work is performed by or on the system (W = ∫ P dV = 0).

title: For an ideal gas, the relationship between molar heat capacity at constant pressure (Cp) and constant volume (Cv) is given by Mayer's relation as:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Mayer's relation Cp - Cv = R reflects the additional energy required at constant pressure to do expansion work against atmospheric pressure.

title: The ratio of specific heat capacities γ = Cp / Cv for a standard monoatomic ideal gas (such as Helium or Argon) is approximately:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: For a monoatomic gas with 3 translational degrees of freedom, Cv = 3/2 R and Cp = 5/2 R, so γ = (5/2) / (3/2) = 5/3 ≈ 1.67.

title: For a diatomic ideal gas (such as Nitrogen or Oxygen) at room temperature, the adiabatic index γ = Cp / Cv is approximately:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: At room temperature, diatomic molecules have 3 translational and 2 rotational degrees of freedom (5 total), yielding Cv = 5/2 R, Cp = 7/2 R, and γ = 7/5 = 1.40.

title: During a reversible adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas, the pressure P and volume V satisfy which relation?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The Poisson equation for a reversible adiabatic process is P * V^γ = constant, where γ is the heat capacity ratio Cp/Cv.

title: What is the unique thermodynamic state at which water can coexist stably in solid, liquid, and vapor phases simultaneously in equilibrium?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: The Triple Point of Water (0.01 °C and 611.65 Pa)
The Boiling Point of Water (100 °C at 1 atm)
The Critical Point of Water (374 °C and 22.06 MPa)

explanation: Water's triple point occurs at precisely 273.16 K (0.01 °C) and 611.657 Pa (0.006 atm), serving as an international temperature standard.

title: Beyond which thermodynamic temperature and pressure does the distinction between the liquid and gas phases of a substance disappear into a supercritical fluid?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Beyond the critical point (critical temperature Tc and critical pressure Pc), liquid and gas merge into a single homogeneous supercritical phase.

title: Fourier's Law of Thermal Conduction states that the rate of heat transfer (Q/t) through a planar slab of material is directly proportional to:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: The square of the slab thickness

explanation: Fourier's Law states dQ/dt = -k * A * (dT/dx), where k is thermal conductivity, A is surface area, and dT/dx is the temperature gradient.

title: Stefan-Boltzmann Law states that the total radiant power emitted per unit surface area of an ideal blackbody is proportional to:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: The fourth power of absolute temperature (T^4)

explanation: The Stefan-Boltzmann law states P/A = σ * T^4, where σ = 5.67 x 10^-8 W/(m^2*K^4) is the Stefan-Boltzmann constant.

title: Wien's Displacement Law relates the peak emission wavelength (λ_max) of a blackbody to its absolute temperature T according to:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Wien's law states λ_max * T = b (where b ≈ 2.898 x 10^-3 m*K). As temperature rises, peak radiation shifts to shorter wavelengths.

title: Newton's Law of Cooling states that the rate of heat loss from a warm body is directly proportional to:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: The temperature difference between the body and its surroundings
The square root of absolute temperature
The latent heat of the cooling fluid

explanation: Newton's Law of Cooling expresses dQ/dt = -h * A * (T_body - T_env), valid for modest temperature differentials.

title: Which mode of heat transfer involves the macroscopic physical movement of heated fluid mass from one region to another?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Convection transfers thermal energy via fluid bulk flow driven by buoyancy differences (natural) or pumps/fans (forced).

title: Which mode of heat transfer requires no physical matter or intervening medium, allowing solar energy to traverse the vacuum of space?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Thermal radiation propagates as electromagnetic waves (primarily infrared) and travels unhindered through vacuum at the speed of light.

title: The root-mean-square (rms) speed of molecules of an ideal gas of molar mass M at absolute temperature T is given by:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Kinetic theory equates (1/2) M v_rms^2 = (3/2) RT, yielding v_rms = √(3RT/M).

title: In Maxwell-Boltzmann molecular speed distribution, which speed value is numerically the smallest among the characteristic speeds of gas molecules?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Speed of sound in the gas

explanation: For an ideal gas: v_mp = √(2RT/M) < v_avg = √(8RT/πM) < v_rms = √(3RT/M). The most probable speed is the smallest.

title: The coefficient of volumetric thermal expansion (β) for an isotropic solid material is approximately related to its linear expansion coefficient (α) by:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: For an isotropic solid expanding equally in all three dimensions, dV/V ≈ 3 (dL/L), so β ≈ 3α.

title: When ice melts into liquid water at 0 °C at standard atmospheric pressure, its physical volume:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Water exhibits anomalous expansion: ice has an open hexagonal cage structure that collapses upon melting, making liquid water denser than ice.

title: At what temperature does pure liquid water attain its maximum density under standard atmospheric pressure?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Water reaches its maximum density of 1.000 g/cm³ at approximately 3.98 °C (4 °C), preventing lakes from freezing solid to the bottom.

title: The quantity of heat required to raise the temperature of 1 gram of pure water by 1 degree Celsius (from 14.5 °C to 15.5 °C) is defined as:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: 1 calorie is defined as 4.184 Joules, the specific heat capacity of liquid water at 15 °C.

title: In the Joule-Thomson expansion (throttling process) of a real gas through an insulated porous plug, which thermodynamic property remains strictly constant?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Throttling is an isenthalpic process (ΔH = 0). Whether a real gas cools or warms depends on whether its temperature is below its inversion temperature.

title: The temperature above which a real gas cannot be liquefied, no matter how much pressure is applied, is called its:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Above the critical temperature Tc, molecular thermal kinetic energy exceeds intermolecular attractive forces, preventing condensation.

title: In an ideal diesel engine cycle, heat addition from fuel combustion occurs during which thermodynamic process?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The ideal Diesel cycle features constant-pressure (isobaric) heat addition, unlike the Otto cycle which adds heat at constant volume (isochoric).

title: In an ideal Otto engine cycle (gasoline combustion engine), heat addition occurs during which thermodynamic process?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The Otto cycle models spark-ignition gasoline engines with constant-volume (isochoric) heat addition during fuel combustion.

title: For Helium, which is a monoatomic gas, what is the theoretical molar heat capacity at constant volume (Cv) according to equipartition theorem?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: By the equipartition theorem, each active degree of freedom contributes (1/2) R to the molar heat capacity Cv. For Helium (monoatomic), Cv = 3/2 R.

title: For Argon, which is a monoatomic gas, what is the theoretical molar heat capacity at constant volume (Cv) according to equipartition theorem?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: By the equipartition theorem, each active degree of freedom contributes (1/2) R to the molar heat capacity Cv. For Argon (monoatomic), Cv = 3/2 R.

title: For Neon, which is a monoatomic gas, what is the theoretical molar heat capacity at constant volume (Cv) according to equipartition theorem?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: By the equipartition theorem, each active degree of freedom contributes (1/2) R to the molar heat capacity Cv. For Neon (monoatomic), Cv = 3/2 R.

title: For Nitrogen (N2), which is a diatomic gas, what is the theoretical molar heat capacity at constant volume (Cv) according to equipartition theorem?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: By the equipartition theorem, each active degree of freedom contributes (1/2) R to the molar heat capacity Cv. For Nitrogen (N2) (diatomic), Cv = 5/2 R.

title: For Oxygen (O2), which is a diatomic gas, what is the theoretical molar heat capacity at constant volume (Cv) according to equipartition theorem?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: By the equipartition theorem, each active degree of freedom contributes (1/2) R to the molar heat capacity Cv. For Oxygen (O2) (diatomic), Cv = 5/2 R.

title: For Hydrogen (H2), which is a diatomic gas, what is the theoretical molar heat capacity at constant volume (Cv) according to equipartition theorem?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: By the equipartition theorem, each active degree of freedom contributes (1/2) R to the molar heat capacity Cv. For Hydrogen (H2) (diatomic), Cv = 5/2 R.

title: For Carbon Dioxide (CO2), which is a triatomic linear gas, what is the theoretical molar heat capacity at constant volume (Cv) according to equipartition theorem?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: By the equipartition theorem, each active degree of freedom contributes (1/2) R to the molar heat capacity Cv. For Carbon Dioxide (CO2) (triatomic linear), Cv = 7/2 R.

title: For Water Vapor (H2O), which is a triatomic non-linear gas, what is the theoretical molar heat capacity at constant volume (Cv) according to equipartition theorem?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: By the equipartition theorem, each active degree of freedom contributes (1/2) R to the molar heat capacity Cv. For Water Vapor (H2O) (triatomic non-linear), Cv = 3 R.

title: A reversible Carnot heat engine operates between a heat source at 800 K and a heat sink at 400 K. What is its thermal efficiency?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Carnot efficiency is η = 1 - (T_cold / T_hot) = 1 - (400 / 800) = 50%.

title: A reversible Carnot heat engine operates between a heat source at 500 K and a heat sink at 250 K. What is its thermal efficiency?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Carnot efficiency is η = 1 - (T_cold / T_hot) = 1 - (250 / 500) = 50%.

title: A reversible Carnot heat engine operates between a heat source at 900 K and a heat sink at 300 K. What is its thermal efficiency?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Carnot efficiency is η = 1 - (T_cold / T_hot) = 1 - (300 / 900) = 66.7%.

title: A reversible Carnot heat engine operates between a heat source at 1000 K and a heat sink at 200 K. What is its thermal efficiency?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Carnot efficiency is η = 1 - (T_cold / T_hot) = 1 - (200 / 1000) = 80%.

title: A reversible Carnot heat engine operates between a heat source at 400 K and a heat sink at 300 K. What is its thermal efficiency?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Carnot efficiency is η = 1 - (T_cold / T_hot) = 1 - (300 / 400) = 25%.

title: A reversible Carnot heat engine operates between a heat source at 600 K and a heat sink at 450 K. What is its thermal efficiency?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Carnot efficiency is η = 1 - (T_cold / T_hot) = 1 - (450 / 600) = 25%.

title: A reversible Carnot heat engine operates between a heat source at 750 K and a heat sink at 250 K. What is its thermal efficiency?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Carnot efficiency is η = 1 - (T_cold / T_hot) = 1 - (250 / 750) = 66.7%.

title: A reversible Carnot heat engine operates between a heat source at 1200 K and a heat sink at 300 K. What is its thermal efficiency?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Carnot efficiency is η = 1 - (T_cold / T_hot) = 1 - (300 / 1200) = 75%.

title: What is the theoretical maximum Coefficient of Performance (COP) of a Carnot refrigerator operating between an interior temperature of 250 K and room temperature of 300 K?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The COP of a Carnot refrigerator is COP = T_cold / (T_hot - T_cold) = 250 / (300 - 250) = 5.0.

title: What is the theoretical maximum Coefficient of Performance (COP) of a Carnot refrigerator operating between an interior temperature of 260 K and room temperature of 290 K?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The COP of a Carnot refrigerator is COP = T_cold / (T_hot - T_cold) = 260 / (290 - 260) = 8.67.

title: What is the theoretical maximum Coefficient of Performance (COP) of a Carnot refrigerator operating between an interior temperature of 240 K and room temperature of 300 K?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The COP of a Carnot refrigerator is COP = T_cold / (T_hot - T_cold) = 240 / (300 - 240) = 4.0.

title: What is the theoretical maximum Coefficient of Performance (COP) of a Carnot refrigerator operating between an interior temperature of 270 K and room temperature of 310 K?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The COP of a Carnot refrigerator is COP = T_cold / (T_hot - T_cold) = 270 / (310 - 270) = 6.75.

title: What is the theoretical maximum Coefficient of Performance (COP) of a Carnot refrigerator operating between an interior temperature of 240 K and room temperature of 280 K?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The COP of a Carnot refrigerator is COP = T_cold / (T_hot - T_cold) = 240 / (280 - 240) = 6.0.

title: What is the theoretical maximum Coefficient of Performance (COP) of a Carnot refrigerator operating between an interior temperature of 270 K and room temperature of 300 K?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The COP of a Carnot refrigerator is COP = T_cold / (T_hot - T_cold) = 270 / (300 - 270) = 9.0.

title: What is the SI unit of entropy?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Entropy has dimensions of energy divided by temperature, with SI units J/K.

title: When a real gas undergoes free expansion into a vacuum inside an insulated vessel, the work done (W) is:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Free expansion involves no resisting opposing force (P_ext = 0), so W = ∫ P_ext dV = 0.

title: Which thermodynamic potential is minimized when a system reaches equilibrium at constant temperature and pressure?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: At constant temperature and pressure, spontaneous processes minimize Gibbs free energy (dG ≤ 0).

title: At constant temperature and volume, which thermodynamic potential reaches a minimum at equilibrium?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: At constant T and V, spontaneous processes minimize Helmholtz free energy A = U - TS.

title: What is the efficiency of a hypothetical perpetual motion machine of the second kind (PMM-2)?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Violates the Second Law by converting 100% of absorbed heat into work without a cold sink
Produces energy from nothing violating the First Law
Reaches absolute zero temperature in finite steps

explanation: A PMM-2 absorbs heat from a single reservoir and converts it completely into work, violating Kelvin-Planck's statement.

title: In heat transfer, the dimensionless Biot number (Bi) compares:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Internal conductive thermal resistance to surface convective thermal resistance
Buoyancy forces to viscous forces in natural convection
Inertial forces to viscous forces in pipe flow

explanation: Bi = (h * L_c) / k compares surface convection resistance to internal conduction resistance.

title: In fluid heat transfer, the dimensionless Prandtl number (Pr) is the ratio of:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Kinematic viscosity (momentum diffusivity) to thermal diffusivity
Convective heat transfer to conductive heat transfer
Radiation heat flux to conduction flux

explanation: Pr = ν / α = (μ * Cp) / k, linking velocity boundary layer thickness to thermal boundary layer thickness.

title: The Clausius-Clapeyron equation describes the relationship between:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Vapor pressure of a substance and its absolute temperature during phase transition
Thermal expansion and electrical resistivity of metals
Internal energy and volume in an isochoric chamber

explanation: The Clausius-Clapeyron equation dP/dT = L / (T * ΔV) models the slope of liquid-vapor and solid-vapor coexistence curves.

title: In calorimetry, the water equivalent of a calorimeter is defined as:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: The mass of water that absorbs the same amount of heat as the calorimeter for an equal rise in temperature
The total volume of distilled water held inside the inner cup
The ratio of thermal conductivity of copper to water
The latent heat of fusion of the insulating jacket

explanation: Water equivalent w = m_cal * c_cal / c_water, expressing calorimeter thermal capacity in grams of water.

title: What happens to the temperature of a gas when it expands adiabatically against external pressure?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Work is performed at the expense of internal energy (ΔU = -W), reducing the temperature of the gas.

title: What happens to the temperature of a gas when it is compressed adiabatically?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Work is done on the gas (+W), increasing its internal energy and temperature.

title: Which statement correctly reflects the Kelvin-Planck statement of the Second Law of Thermodynamics?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: It is impossible to construct an engine operating in a cycle whose sole effect is to extract heat from a reservoir and perform an equivalent amount of work
Heat can spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body without external work
Entropy of any closed system decreases during spontaneous processes
Energy cannot be transformed from one form to another

explanation: The Kelvin-Planck statement establishes that no heat engine can have an efficiency of 100%.

title: Which statement correctly reflects the Clausius statement of the Second Law of Thermodynamics?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: It is impossible to construct a cyclic device whose sole effect is the transfer of heat from a cooler body to a warmer body
Total energy in any isolated system is conserved
Entropy reaches infinity at the triple point
Work cannot be completely converted into heat

explanation: The Clausius statement dictates that refrigeration requires an external input of work.

title: In a closed thermodynamic cycle plotted on a Pressure-Volume (P-V) diagram, the net work performed per cycle equals:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: The area enclosed by the cycle curve
The slope of the adiabat at the midpoint
The volume at maximum pressure minus volume at minimum pressure
The total perimeter of the cycle

explanation: On a P-V diagram, work is W = ∮ P dV, which geometrically represents the enclosed area.

title: In a closed thermodynamic cycle plotted on a Temperature-Entropy (T-S) diagram, the net work done equals:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: The area enclosed by the cycle curve
The maximum temperature multiplied by minimum entropy
The slope of the isochoric path

explanation: On a T-S diagram, Q_net = ∮ T dS = W_net, so the enclosed area equals the net work done per cycle.

title: The molar latent heat of vaporization of water at 100 °C is approximately:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Water requires ~2260 J/g (40.7 kJ/mol) to transition from liquid to steam, reflecting extensive hydrogen bonding.

title: The molar latent heat of fusion of ice at 0 °C is approximately:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Melting ice at 0 °C requires 334 J/g (6.01 kJ/mol) of heat without any change in temperature.

title: What is the value of absolute zero on the Celsius scale?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: 0 Kelvin corresponds precisely to -273.15 °C.

title: Which thermodynamic law provides the basis for defining temperature scales objectively?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The Zeroth Law establishes thermal equilibrium as a transitive relation, enabling the definition of temperature.

title: When two blocks of identical mass and specific heat capacity at temperatures T1 and T2 are brought into thermal contact in an isolated system, the final equilibrium temperature is:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Conservation of thermal energy requires m*c*(T_f - T1) + m*c*(T_f - T2) = 0, giving T_f = (T1 + T2)/2.

title: In the previous thermal mixing problem, the total entropy change of the isolated two-block system (ΔS_total) is:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Zero because heat lost equals heat gained

explanation: Heat transfer across a finite temperature difference is irreversible, so ΔS = m*c*ln((T1+T2)^2 / (4*T1*T2)) > 0.

title: The van der Waals equation of state [P + a(n/V)^2] * (V - nb) = nRT corrects the ideal gas law by accounting for:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Intermolecular attraction forces ('a') and finite molecular volume ('b')
Nuclear relativistic mass increase and spin coupling

explanation: Parameter 'a' accounts for dipole/dispersion attractions reducing wall pressure, and 'b' is the excluded volume occupied by molecules.

title: In thermal physics, the concept of 'degrees of freedom' refers to:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: The number of independent coordinates or quadratic terms required to specify the energy of a molecule
The number of phase transitions a substance can undergo
The number of moles per unit volume of gas
The ratio of atmospheric pressure to gauge pressure

explanation: Each translational, rotational, or vibrational mode that can store energy is a degree of freedom.

title: At very high temperatures, vibrational modes become active in diatomic gases, adding how many additional quadratic energy terms to the molar heat capacity Cv?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: A vibrational mode possesses both kinetic energy (1/2 μ v^2) and potential energy (1/2 k x^2), contributing 2 * (1/2 R) = R to Cv.

title: The Dulong-Petit Law states that the molar heat capacity of most solid elemental crystalline metals at room temperature is approximately:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: In 3D crystalline solids, atoms vibrate as 3D harmonic oscillators with 6 degrees of freedom, giving Cv = 3R ≈ 25 J/(mol·K).

title: Einstein and Debye models of specific heat explained why the heat capacity of solids drops to zero as temperature approaches 0 K, proportional to:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: T^3 (at low temperatures in Debye model)

explanation: Debye's model treats lattice vibrations as quantized acoustic phonons, predicting Cv ∝ T^3 at low temperatures, matching experiments.

title: Which temperature scale has the same incremental degree interval as the Fahrenheit scale, but starts at absolute zero?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The Rankine scale sets 0 °R at absolute zero, with 1 °R = 1 °F. Water freezes at 491.67 °R and boils at 671.67 °R.

title: An ideal gas expands from 1 m³ to 3 m³ at a constant pressure of 200 kPa. What is the total work done by the gas?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: For isobaric expansion, W = P * ΔV = 200,000 Pa * (3 - 1) m³ = 400,000 J = 400 kJ.

title: If an ideal gas absorbs 500 J of heat and simultaneously does 200 J of expansion work on its surroundings, what is the change in its internal energy (ΔU)?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: According to the First Law: ΔU = Q - W = 500 J - 200 J = +300 J.

title: In an isochoric heating process, 800 J of heat is added to a sealed rigid container of gas. What is the work done by the gas?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Because volume is rigid and constant (ΔV = 0), work done is W = P * ΔV = 0 J. All heat added goes into increasing internal energy.

title: A heat engine absorbs 1,000 J of heat from a hot reservoir and exhausts 600 J of heat to a cold reservoir in each cycle. What is its thermal efficiency?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Thermal efficiency is η = W / Q_in = (Q_in - Q_out) / Q_in = (1000 - 600) / 1000 = 400 / 1000 = 0.40 or 40%.

title: A heat pump delivers 5,000 J of heat to warm a house while consuming 1,000 J of electrical work. What is its Coefficient of Performance (COP_heating)?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: COP_heating = Q_delivered / W_electric = 5000 J / 1000 J = 5.0.

title: What is the thermal resistance R_th of a 0.05-meter-thick insulating board with thermal conductivity k = 0.04 W/(m·K) and surface area A = 2 m²?
subject: Physical Sciences

title: In radiation, an object that absorbs 100% of all incident electromagnetic radiation without reflection or transmission is termed a:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: An ideal blackbody has an absorptivity α = 1 across all wavelengths and is also an ideal emitter (emissivity ε = 1).

title: Kirchhoff's Law of Thermal Radiation states that at thermal equilibrium, for any body at a given temperature:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Emissivity is inversely proportional to reflectance
Total radiated power is independent of wavelength
Absorptivity is zero in infrared wavelengths

explanation: Good absorbers are equally good emitters: a surface that absorbs radiation well also radiates energy efficiently at that wavelength.

title: A domestic heat radiator painted matte black cools faster by radiation than an identical one painted glossy white because:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Matte black has a much higher emissivity (ε ≈ 0.95)
Black paint conducts heat 10 times faster than white paint
Matte surfaces prevent air molecule contact

explanation: Emissivity determines radiation rate: matte black surfaces have ε near 1.0, while polished white/metallic surfaces have much lower emissivity.

title: If the absolute temperature of a radiating blackbody is doubled from 300 K to 600 K, its total emitted radiant power increases by a factor of:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: By the Stefan-Boltzmann law P ∝ T^4, doubling absolute temperature multiplies radiated power by 2^4 = 16.

title: If the surface temperature of a star is 6,000 K, at what approximate wavelength does its radiation spectrum peak (using Wien's constant b ≈ 3 x 10^-3 m·K)?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: By Wien's law: λ_max = b / T = (3 x 10^-3 m·K) / 6000 K = 5 x 10^-7 m = 500 nm.

title: During a phase change (such as water boiling at 100 °C), what happens to the temperature of the substance while heat is continuously supplied?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: It rises linearly with heat input
It drops slightly due to vaporization cooling
It fluctuates wildly around the critical point

explanation: Supplied latent heat is used entirely to break intermolecular hydrogen bonds rather than increasing average kinetic energy.

title: The concept of 'latent heat' was discovered and named in the 18th century by which Scottish chemist?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Joseph Black distinguished between temperature (heat intensity) and latent heat absorbed during phase changes.

title: What is the mechanical equivalent of heat, experimentally determined by James Prescott Joule using paddle wheels in water?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Joule's paddle-wheel experiment demonstrated that 4.18 Joules of mechanical work consistently raises 1 gram of water by 1 °C.

title: In an adiabatic demagnetization cooling process, ultra-low temperatures near absolute zero are reached by:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Aligning magnetic dipoles in a paramagnetic salt and then adiabatically removing the magnetic field
Compressing liquid helium past its lambda transition
Vaporizing solid mercury in an electric arc
Expanding nitrogen gas through a supersonic de Laval nozzle

explanation: Adiabatic demagnetization cools paramagnetic salts to millikelvin temperatures by forcing thermal energy into magnetic dipole randomization.

title: An ideal gas sample absorbs heat at constant pressure, raising its temperature from 1250 K to 1300 K. Which thermodynamic law dictates that the heat absorbed equals the change in enthalpy (Q_p = ΔH)?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: First Law of Thermodynamics applied to an isobaric system

explanation: At constant pressure, enthalpy H = U + PV, so dH = dU + P dV = dQ_p. Thus heat exchanged isobarically equals change in enthalpy.

title: An ideal gas sample absorbs heat at constant pressure, raising its temperature from 1260 K to 1310 K. Which thermodynamic law dictates that the heat absorbed equals the change in enthalpy (Q_p = ΔH)?
subject: Physical Sciences

explanation: At constant pressure, enthalpy H = U + PV, so dH = dU + P dV = dQ_p. Thus heat exchanged isobarically equals change in enthalpy.

explanation: At constant pressure, enthalpy H = U + PV, so dH = dU + P dV = dQ_p. Thus heat exchanged isobarically equals change in enthalpy.

explanation: At constant pressure, enthalpy H = U + PV, so dH = dU + P dV = dQ_p. Thus heat exchanged isobarically equals change in enthalpy.

subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: First Law of Thermodynamics applied to an isobaric system

explanation: At constant pressure, enthalpy H = U + PV, so dH = dU + P dV = dQ_p. Thus heat exchanged isobarically equals change in enthalpy.

explanation: At constant pressure, enthalpy H = U + PV, so dH = dU + P dV = dQ_p. Thus heat exchanged isobarically equals change in enthalpy.

title: An ideal gas sample absorbs heat at constant pressure, raising its temperature from 1350 K to 1400 K. Which thermodynamic law dictates that the heat absorbed equals the change in enthalpy (Q_p = ΔH)?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: First Law of Thermodynamics applied to an isobaric system

explanation: At constant pressure, enthalpy H = U + PV, so dH = dU + P dV = dQ_p. Thus heat exchanged isobarically equals change in enthalpy.

title: Coulomb's Law states that the electrostatic force between two point charges q1 and q2 separated by distance r is proportional to:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Coulomb's Law F = k * |q1 * q2| / r^2 describes the inverse-square electrostatic force between two stationary electric charges.

title: What is the SI unit of electric capacitance?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Capacitance is measured in Farads (F), where 1 Farad = 1 Coulomb per Volt (1 C/V).

title: The energy U stored in a capacitor of capacitance C charged to a potential difference V is given by:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The electrostatic potential energy stored in the electric field between capacitor plates is U = (1/2) Q V = (1/2) C V^2.

title: What happens to the capacitance of an isolated parallel plate capacitor when a dielectric material with dielectric constant κ is inserted between its plates?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Capacitance increases by a factor of κ
Capacitance decreases by a factor of κ

explanation: A dielectric polarizes in the electric field, reducing internal field strength and increasing capacitance to C = κ * C0.

title: According to Ohm's Law (V = I * R), the electrical resistance R of a uniform cylindrical conducting wire of length L and cross-sectional area A is:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Resistance is directly proportional to length L and resistivity ρ, and inversely proportional to cross-sectional area A.

title: Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL), stating that the sum of currents entering any circuit junction equals the sum of currents leaving it, is a direct consequence of:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: KCL reflects the principle that electric charge cannot accumulate indefinitely at a junction node in a steady-state circuit.

title: Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL), stating that the directed sum of potential differences around any closed circuit loop is zero, is a direct consequence of:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: KVL expresses conservation of energy in electrostatic fields: traveling in a complete closed loop returns the potential to its starting value.

title: In an electrical circuit, two resistors of resistance R1 = 6 Ω and R2 = 3 Ω connected in parallel have an equivalent resistance of:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: For parallel resistors: 1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 = 1/6 + 1/3 = 3/6 = 1/2, so R_eq = 2 Ω.

title: Two capacitors of capacitance C1 = 4 μF and C2 = 6 μF connected in parallel have an equivalent capacitance of:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Capacitors in parallel add directly: C_eq = C1 + C2 = 4 + 6 = 10 μF.

title: Two capacitors of capacitance C1 = 6 μF and C2 = 3 μF connected in series have an equivalent capacitance of:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: For series capacitors: 1/C_eq = 1/C1 + 1/C2 = 1/6 + 1/3 = 3/6 = 1/2, so C_eq = 2 μF.

title: What is the characteristic time constant τ of a series resistor-capacitor (RC) circuit containing resistance R and capacitance C?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The time constant τ = R * C represents the time required for capacitor voltage to charge to ~63.2% of its maximum value.

title: What is the characteristic time constant τ of a series inductor-resistor (RL) circuit containing resistance R and inductance L?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: In an RL circuit, τ = L / R represents the time taken for current to rise to (1 - 1/e) ≈ 63.2% of its steady-state value.

title: What is the resonant angular frequency ω0 of a series RLC circuit containing inductance L and capacitance C?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: At resonance, inductive reactance X_L = ωL cancels capacitive reactance X_C = 1/(ωC), giving ω0 = 1/√(LC).

title: What is the SI unit of magnetic flux?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Magnetic flux Φ_B = ∫ B · dA is measured in Webers (Wb), where 1 Wb = 1 Tesla · meter².

title: What is the SI unit of magnetic field strength (magnetic flux density B)?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Magnetic field B is measured in Tesla (T) in SI units, where 1 Tesla = 1 N / (A · m) = 10,000 Gauss.

title: Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction states that the magnitude of the induced electromotive force (EMF) in a circuit is proportional to:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: The time rate of change of magnetic flux through the circuit
The total electrostatic charge on the conductor
The resistance of the wire loop
The electrostatic potential of the surrounding air

explanation: Faraday's Law states ε = -dΦ_B/dt: an induced EMF is generated by any temporal change in magnetic flux linking the circuit.

title: Lenz's Law, reflected by the negative sign in Faraday's equation (ε = -dΦ/dt), states that an induced electric current always flows in a direction such that:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Its magnetic field opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it
It reinforces the original magnetic field causing runaway current
It converts electrical energy into mass
It eliminates all electrical resistance in the circuit

explanation: Lenz's Law is a consequence of conservation of energy: the induced current opposes the change in flux to prevent energy creation from nothing.

title: The magnetic force F acting on a particle of charge q moving with velocity v through a magnetic field B is given by the Lorentz force formula:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The magnetic force F = q(v × B) is perpendicular to both velocity and magnetic field, doing zero work on the charged particle.

title: Because the magnetic force on a moving charged particle F = q(v × B) is always perpendicular to its velocity vector v, the magnetic force does:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Zero work on the particle (kinetic energy remains constant)

explanation: Since F ⊥ v, the instantaneous power P = F · v = 0. A static magnetic field changes the direction of motion but never the speed or kinetic energy.

title: When a charged particle of mass m and charge q enters a uniform magnetic field B perpendicular to its velocity v, it moves in a circle with radius:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Equating centripetal force m*v^2/r to magnetic force q*v*B yields the cyclotron radius r = m*v / (q*B).

title: The cyclotron frequency (gyrofrequency) f_c of a charged particle orbiting in a uniform magnetic field B is independent of which variable?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Speed and orbital radius of the particle

explanation: Cyclotron frequency f_c = qB / (2πm) is independent of particle speed v and radius r at non-relativistic velocities.

title: Ampère's Circuital Law states that the line integral of magnetic field B around any closed loop equals μ0 multiplied by:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: The total electric current enclosed by the loop
The total electric charge enclosed by the loop
The rate of change of magnetic flux
The voltage drop across the loop

explanation: Ampere's Law ∮ B · dl = μ0 * I_enc relates the circulating magnetic field to the net macroscopic current passing through the loop.

title: James Clerk Maxwell modified Ampère's Law by introducing which term to account for time-varying electric fields producing magnetic fields?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Maxwell realized that charging capacitors create magnetic fields even in vacuum, introducing displacement current to achieve electromagnetic symmetry.

title: The magnetic field B at the center of a long, tightly wound solenoid having n turns per unit length carrying current I is given by:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Inside an ideal long solenoid, the magnetic field is uniform and directed along the axis with magnitude B = μ0 * n * I.

title: The Hall Effect refers to the production of a transverse voltage difference across an electrical conductor carrying current when placed in:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The Hall Effect arises when magnetic force deflects charge carriers toward one edge of the conductor, revealing carrier charge sign and density.

title: In an ideal electrical transformer with primary turns Np and secondary turns Ns, the ratio of secondary voltage Vs to primary voltage Vp is:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: By Faraday's Law, the induced EMF per turn is identical in both windings, giving Vs / Vp = Ns / Np.

title: In a step-up transformer where secondary voltage is higher than primary voltage (Vs > Vp), the secondary current Is compared to primary current Ip is:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Lower (Is < Ip) to conserve electrical power

explanation: Conservation of energy requires ideal power equality: P_in = P_out, so Vp * Ip = Vs * Is. Stepping up voltage steps down current.

title: Eddy currents induced in the solid iron cores of transformers and electric motors are minimized by:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Using laminated sheets insulated from one another
Increasing the core temperature to red heat
Operating the transformer with direct current
Using solid copper blocks as the magnetic core

explanation: Laminating the magnetic core into thin sheets separated by varnish prevents large circulating eddy current loops, reducing I^2*R heat losses.

title: What is the root-mean-square (RMS) voltage of a standard sinusoidal household AC voltage with a peak voltage V0 of 325 Volts?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: For a sine wave, V_rms = V0 / √2 ≈ 0.707 * V0. For V0 = 325 V, V_rms ≈ 230 V.

title: In a purely inductive AC circuit where voltage V = V0 * sin(ωt), the electric current I:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Lags behind the voltage by 90° (π/2 radians)
Is exactly in phase with the voltage
Lags behind the voltage by 180° (π radians)

explanation: In an inductor, back-EMF opposes current growth, causing current to lag 90° behind voltage ('ELI the ICE man').

title: Two resistors of 10 Ω and 10 Ω are connected in parallel across an ideal battery. What is their combined equivalent resistance?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: For parallel resistors 1/R_eq = 1/10 + 1/10, which calculates to 5 Ω.

title: Two resistors of 12 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in parallel across an ideal battery. What is their combined equivalent resistance?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: For parallel resistors 1/R_eq = 1/12 + 1/6, which calculates to 4 Ω.

title: Two resistors of 20 Ω and 5 Ω are connected in parallel across an ideal battery. What is their combined equivalent resistance?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: For parallel resistors 1/R_eq = 1/20 + 1/5, which calculates to 4 Ω.

title: Two resistors of 30 Ω and 20 Ω are connected in parallel across an ideal battery. What is their combined equivalent resistance?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: For parallel resistors 1/R_eq = 1/30 + 1/20, which calculates to 12 Ω.

title: Two resistors of 100 Ω and 100 Ω are connected in parallel across an ideal battery. What is their combined equivalent resistance?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: For parallel resistors 1/R_eq = 1/100 + 1/100, which calculates to 50 Ω.

title: Two resistors of 40 Ω and 60 Ω are connected in parallel across an ideal battery. What is their combined equivalent resistance?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: For parallel resistors 1/R_eq = 1/40 + 1/60, which calculates to 24 Ω.

title: Two resistors of 8 Ω and 8 Ω are connected in parallel across an ideal battery. What is their combined equivalent resistance?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: For parallel resistors 1/R_eq = 1/8 + 1/8, which calculates to 4 Ω.

title: Two resistors of 50 Ω and 50 Ω are connected in parallel across an ideal battery. What is their combined equivalent resistance?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: For parallel resistors 1/R_eq = 1/50 + 1/50, which calculates to 25 Ω.

title: Two resistors of 15 Ω and 30 Ω are connected in parallel across an ideal battery. What is their combined equivalent resistance?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: For parallel resistors 1/R_eq = 1/15 + 1/30, which calculates to 10 Ω.

title: Two resistors of 100 Ω and 25 Ω are connected in parallel across an ideal battery. What is their combined equivalent resistance?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: For parallel resistors 1/R_eq = 1/100 + 1/25, which calculates to 20 Ω.

title: In a purely capacitive AC circuit, the electric current:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Is in phase with the voltage

explanation: In a capacitor, charge and current establish before voltage builds up, so current leads voltage by 90°.

title: What is the electrical power factor in an AC circuit where current and voltage are in phase (purely resistive)?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Power factor cos(φ) = cos(0°) = 1.0, meaning all supplied energy is converted into real work or heat.

title: What is the SI unit of electrical inductance?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Inductance is measured in Henries (H), where 1 Henry = 1 Volt · second per Ampere (1 V·s/A).

title: The energy U stored in the magnetic field of an inductor of inductance L carrying current I is:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The energy stored in an inductor's magnetic field is U = (1/2) L I^2.

title: Which law in electrodynamics states that magnetic monopoles do not exist in nature (∇ · B = 0)?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Gauss's Law for magnetism states that magnetic flux through any closed Gaussian surface is zero.

title: What is the speed of electromagnetic waves in a vacuum according to Maxwell's equations?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Maxwell discovered that light speed is determined purely by vacuum permittivity ε0 and permeability μ0.

title: The Poynting vector S in electromagnetism represents:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: The directional energy flux density of an electromagnetic field (S = (1/μ0) E × B)
The electrostatic charge density in a plasma
The mechanical torque on a permanent magnet
The drift velocity of conduction electrons

explanation: The Poynting vector S = (E × B)/μ0 has units of W/m² and points in the direction of electromagnetic energy propagation.

title: What device converts mechanical rotational energy into alternating electrical current using electromagnetic induction?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: An alternator rotates wire coils within a magnetic field, generating alternating electromotive force by Faraday's law.

title: In an electric motor, what component reverses the direction of current in the rotor armature every half turn to maintain continuous rotation in a DC motor?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The split-ring commutator switches current polarity every 180° to ensure torque continues in the same rotational direction.

title: Superconductors exhibit the Meissner effect, which is the phenomenon of:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Complete expulsion of magnetic fields from the interior of the material when in the superconducting state
Infinite electrical resistance at ultra-cold temperatures
Emission of monochromatic laser light under magnetic fields
Spontaneous decay of Cooper pairs into positrons

explanation: Below its critical temperature Tc, a superconductor acts as a perfect diamagnet, completely expelling magnetic flux lines.

title: Materials with negative magnetic susceptibility that are weakly repelled by both poles of a magnet are classified as:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Diamagnetic materials (such as bismuth, copper, water) create an induced magnetic field in opposition to an externally applied magnetic field.

title: Materials with positive magnetic susceptibility containing unpaired electron spins that are weakly attracted to magnetic fields are classified as:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Paramagnetic substances (like aluminum, oxygen) have permanent dipole moments that align weakly with external fields.

title: Iron, Cobalt, and Nickel retain permanent magnetization below their Curie temperature due to spontaneous domain alignment, exhibiting:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Ferromagnetic materials exhibit strong spontaneous magnetization within microscopic domains due to quantum exchange interactions.

title: The temperature above which a ferromagnetic material loses its permanent magnetism and behaves as a simple paramagnet is called the:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Above the Curie temperature T_c, thermal agitation overcomes exchange coupling, destroying magnetic domain alignment.

title: What instrument uses a pivoted coil in a magnetic field to detect and measure very small electric currents?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: A moving-coil galvanometer uses torque τ = N * I * A * B opposed by a restoring spring to measure microamperes.

title: To convert a moving-coil galvanometer into an ammeter capable of measuring large currents, one must connect:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: A low-resistance shunt in parallel with the galvanometer coil
A high resistance in series with the galvanometer coil
A capacitor in series with the coil
An iron core inductor in parallel

explanation: A low-resistance shunt diverts the vast majority of current around the delicate galvanometer movement.

title: To convert a moving-coil galvanometer into a voltmeter capable of measuring large voltages, one must connect:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: A high resistance in series with the galvanometer coil
A low-resistance shunt in parallel with the coil
A step-down transformer across the terminals

explanation: A large series resistor ('multiplier') limits the current through the galvanometer to its full-scale deflection value at maximum voltage.

title: In a Wheatstone Bridge circuit with four resistors P, Q, R, and S, what is the balance condition when no current flows through the galvanometer?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: When P/Q = R/S, the bridge is balanced and potential difference across the central galvanometer is zero.

title: A potentiometer is superior to a standard voltmeter for measuring electromotive force (EMF) of a cell because:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: It draws zero current from the cell at the null balance point
It can measure alternating voltages without rectification
It generates its own internal calibration charge

explanation: At the null point, the potentiometer draws no current, measuring the true open-circuit EMF without internal resistance voltage drop IR.

title: The magnetic force between two parallel straight wires carrying currents in the same direction is:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Currents in the same direction attract each other; currents in opposite directions repel, as defined by Ampere's force law.

title: The SI definition of the Ampere was historically defined based on the magnetic force per unit length between:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Two parallel, infinitely long conductors of negligible cross-section placed 1 meter apart in vacuum
A moving coil in a uniform 1 Tesla field

explanation: 1 Ampere historically produced a force of 2 × 10^-7 N/m between two parallel conductors in vacuum.

title: In electromagnetic theory, what does the Poynting-Robertson effect describe in astronomy?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: The drag force exerted by solar radiation on orbiting interplanetary dust particles, causing them to spiral into the Sun
The deflection of starlight by solar gravity
The splitting of spectral lines in sunspot magnetic fields
The acceleration of solar wind protons by coronal holes

explanation: Photons absorbed and re-emitted by orbiting dust grains create an effective drag that removes orbital angular momentum.

title: What is the drift velocity of conduction electrons in a copper wire carrying typical domestic electric currents?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: A few millimeters per second (very slow)
The speed of sound in copper (5,000 m/s)
Zero because electrons do not physically travel

explanation: While the electric field signal propagates near the speed of light, actual electron drift velocity is tiny—typically ~0.1 to 1 mm/s.

title: When electric current passes through a junction of two dissimilar metals, heat is either absorbed or released depending on current direction. This is:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The Peltier effect is the thermoelectric counterpart of the Seebeck effect, utilized in solid-state thermoelectric coolers.

title: The generation of an electromotive force (EMF) across a thermocouple circuit when its two junctions are maintained at different temperatures is:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Thomas Johann Seebeck discovered that temperature differences between dissimilar metal junctions generate electric voltage.

title: Which type of electric current is produced by chemical batteries and solar photovoltaic cells?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Batteries and solar cells produce unidirectional Direct Current (DC).

title: What is the frequency of standard alternating current (AC) electrical power supplied to domestic households in India and Europe?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: India, Europe, and most of Asia/Africa use 50 Hz AC, while North America uses 60 Hz AC.

title: An electric heater rated at 2,000 Watts is operated for 5 hours. How much electrical energy does it consume in kilowatt-hours (units)?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Energy = Power * Time = 2 kW * 5 h = 10 kWh.

title: What safety device installed in residential electrical panels automatically trips and interrupts the circuit when excessive current flows?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: An MCB automatically disconnects power via bimetallic thermal trip or electromagnetic coil when overcurrent or short circuit occurs.

title: Residual Current Devices (RCD) or Earth Leakage Circuit Breakers (ELCB) protect humans from electric shock by detecting:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: An imbalance between live (phase) and neutral currents
High ambient temperature in the fuse box
Low power factor in home appliances

explanation: An RCD detects when current leaking to earth causes phase current to exceed neutral current by as little as 30 mA, tripping in milliseconds.

title: In an electromagnetic wave traveling through free space, the electric field vector E and magnetic field vector B are oriented:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Perpendicular to each other and perpendicular to the direction of propagation
Parallel to each other and parallel to wave propagation
At an angle of 45° to each other

explanation: Electromagnetic waves are transverse: E ⊥ B ⊥ v_prop.

title: The ratio of the electric field amplitude E0 to magnetic field amplitude B0 in an electromagnetic wave in vacuum equals:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: The speed of light c (E0 / B0 = c)

explanation: In free space, E0 / B0 = c = 3.00 × 10^8 m/s.

title: What property of an inductor causes it to oppose any sudden change in electric current flowing through it?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: By Lenz's law, changing current induces a self-induced back-EMF ε = -L (dI/dt) opposing the change.

title: Two coaxial circular coils placed close together share an inductive coupling. The ratio of induced EMF in the secondary coil to current change in primary is:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Mutual inductance M relates induced voltage in one circuit to the rate of change of current in an adjacent circuit (ε2 = -M dI1/dt).

title: Which instrument is used to measure unknown electrical resistance with extreme precision by comparing potential drop along a uniform slide wire?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: A slide-wire potentiometer balances unknown potential drops against a calibrated voltage gradient without drawing current.

title: What is the magnetic field inside the central hollow core of an ideal toroidal solenoid?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Uniform and equal to μ0 * n * I

explanation: By Ampère's law, the magnetic field outside the windings (both in the central empty hole and external space) is zero.

title: Which phenomenon causes high-frequency alternating currents to flow predominantly near the outer surface of a conductor rather than uniformly through its core?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Eddy currents induced by changing magnetic fields inside the conductor oppose current at the center, pushing current to the outer perimeter.

title: In an AC circuit containing only a capacitor, what is the capacitive reactance X_C when AC frequency f approaches zero (direct current)?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: X_C = 1 / (2π f C). As frequency f → 0, X_C → ∞, meaning capacitors completely block direct current (DC).

title: In an electrical circuit, a steady potential difference of 30 Volts is maintained across a resistor of resistance 6 Ohms. According to Ohm's Law (I = V / R), what is the current?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: According to Ohm's Law, current I = V / R = 30 V / 6 Ω = 5.0 A.

title: In an electrical circuit, a steady potential difference of 36 Volts is maintained across a resistor of resistance 7 Ohms. According to Ohm's Law (I = V / R), what is the current?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: According to Ohm's Law, current I = V / R = 36 V / 7 Ω = 5.1 A.

subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: According to Ohm's Law, current I = V / R = 42 V / 8 Ω = 5.3 A.

subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: According to Ohm's Law, current I = V / R = 6 V / 2 Ω = 3.0 A.

explanation: According to Ohm's Law, current I = V / R = 18 V / 4 Ω = 4.5 A.

explanation: According to Ohm's Law, current I = V / R = 24 V / 5 Ω = 4.8 A.

subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: According to Ohm's Law, current I = V / R = 48 V / 9 Ω = 5.3 A.

subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: According to Ohm's Law, current I = V / R = 54 V / 10 Ω = 5.4 A.

subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: According to Ohm's Law, current I = V / R = 60 V / 11 Ω = 5.5 A.

subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: According to Ohm's Law, current I = V / R = 66 V / 2 Ω = 33.0 A.

title: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with an initial velocity of 20 m/s. Assuming g = 10 m/s² and negligible air resistance, what is the maximum height reached?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Using v² = u² - 2gh: at maximum height v = 0, so 0 = (20)² - 2(10)h => 20h = 400 => h = 20 m.

title: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to a speed of 30 m/s in 10 seconds. What is the total distance traveled during this acceleration?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Average velocity v_avg = (0 + 30)/2 = 15 m/s. Distance s = v_avg * t = 15 m/s * 10 s = 150 m.

title: A projectile is launched from flat ground with initial speed v0 at an angle θ to the horizontal. At what launch angle is the horizontal range maximized?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Horizontal range R = (v0² * sin 2θ) / g. Range is maximum when sin 2θ = 1, which occurs at 2θ = 90° or θ = 45°.

title: At the highest point of a parabolic projectile trajectory (ignoring air resistance), what is the velocity of the projectile?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Equal to initial launch velocity v0

explanation: At the apex, the vertical velocity component vy momentarily equals 0, but the horizontal component vx = v0 cos θ remains constant.

title: Newton's Second Law of Motion in its most general and fundamental form states that net external force is equal to:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: The time rate of change of linear momentum (F = dp/dt)
Mass multiplied by constant acceleration (F = ma)
The rate of change of kinetic energy
The product of impulse and displacement

explanation: Newton formulated F = dp/dt = d(mv)/dt, which accounts for both changing velocity and changing mass (such as in rockets).

title: What is the conservation law responsible for the recoil of a firearm when a bullet is shot?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: In an isolated system with no external horizontal force, initial momentum is zero, so p_gun + p_bullet = 0 => p_gun = -p_bullet.

title: In an isolated system, an elastic collision is uniquely characterized by the conservation of both:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Total linear momentum and total kinetic energy
Total linear momentum and total temperature
Total kinetic energy and potential energy only

explanation: Elastic collisions conserve both linear momentum and mechanical kinetic energy, unlike inelastic collisions where kinetic energy is lost as heat/deformation.

title: In a completely inelastic collision between two colliding bodies, what always occurs?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: The colliding bodies stick together and move with a common final velocity
All mechanical kinetic energy is conserved perfectly
The bodies bounce off with equal and opposite speeds
The total linear momentum drops to zero

explanation: In a perfectly inelastic collision, maximum kinetic energy is dissipated and the bodies coalesce into a single combined mass.

title: The coefficient of restitution (e) for a perfectly elastic collision equals:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Coefficient of restitution e = (relative speed of separation) / (relative speed of approach). For perfectly elastic collisions e = 1, and for perfectly inelastic e = 0.

title: What is the work done by centripetal force on an object moving in uniform circular motion?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Equal to (1/2) m v² per revolution
Dependent on the coefficient of friction

explanation: Centripetal force is always directed toward the center, perpendicular to the tangential displacement (F ⊥ ds). Hence W = F · ds = 0.

title: A solid cylinder and a thin-walled hollow hoop of identical mass and radius roll down an inclined plane from rest without slipping. Which reaches the bottom first?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Both reach at the exact same time
Depends on the angle of inclination

explanation: The solid cylinder has a smaller moment of inertia (I = 1/2 MR²) than the hoop (I = MR²), allocating more gravitational potential energy to translational acceleration.

title: What is the moment of inertia of a uniform solid sphere of mass M and radius R about an axis passing through its center?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: By integration, the moment of inertia of a uniform solid sphere about any central diameter is (2/5) M R².

title: What is the moment of inertia of a thin spherical shell (hollow sphere) of mass M and radius R about its diameter?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: A hollow thin-walled spherical shell has all mass concentrated at distance R from the center, yielding I = (2/3) M R².

title: The Parallel Axis Theorem states that the moment of inertia I of a body about any axis parallel to an axis through its center of mass is:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The parallel axis theorem expresses I = I_cm + M*d², where d is the perpendicular distance between the two parallel axes.

title: The Perpendicular Axis Theorem applies strictly to which class of geometric objects?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The perpendicular axis theorem (Iz = Ix + Iy) applies strictly to flat, planar laminas in the xy plane.

title: When a figure skater pulls her arms inward during a spin, her angular speed increases dramatically because:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Her moment of inertia decreases, conserving angular momentum (L = I * ω)
Her gravitational potential energy converts to linear momentum
The centripetal force does positive work on her skates
Friction between ice and blade increases

explanation: With zero external torque (τ = 0), angular momentum L = I * ω is conserved. Decreasing moment of inertia I forces angular speed ω to increase.

title: What is the period T of a simple pendulum of length L in a gravitational field with acceleration g for small angular oscillations?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: For small amplitudes (sin θ ≈ θ), restoring torque yields simple harmonic motion with period T = 2π√(L/g), independent of bob mass.

title: What happens to the period of a simple pendulum if the mass of the hanging bob is doubled?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The period T = 2π√(L/g) depends only on length L and gravitational acceleration g, completely independent of the bob mass.

title: If the length of a simple pendulum is increased by a factor of 4, its period of oscillation will:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Because T ∝ √L, multiplying length by 4 multiplies the period by √4 = 2.

title: In simple harmonic motion (SHM), at what position is the velocity of the oscillating mass at its maximum?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: At equilibrium x = 0, all potential energy is converted into kinetic energy, giving maximum velocity v_max = ω * A.

title: In simple harmonic motion (SHM), at what position is the restoring force and acceleration at its maximum?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Restoring force F = -kx and acceleration a = -ω²x are directly proportional to displacement, peaking at the maximum displacement amplitude x = ±A.

title: What is the total mechanical energy of an undamped mass-spring harmonic oscillator with spring constant k and amplitude A?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Total energy is conserved and equals the maximum potential energy stored at maximum displacement: E = (1/2) k A².

title: Escape velocity from the surface of Earth (ve = √(2GM/R)) is approximately:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: By equating kinetic energy (1/2) m ve² to gravitational binding energy GMm/R, escape velocity from Earth's surface is √(2gR) ≈ 11.2 km/s.

title: Orbital velocity for a satellite in low Earth orbit (LEO, v_orb = √(GM/R)) is approximately:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: In circular orbit, centripetal force equals gravity (m v²/R = GMm/R²), yielding v_orb = √(GM/R) ≈ 7.9 km/s.

title: Kepler's Second Law of Planetary Motion ('equal areas swept in equal times') is a direct consequence of:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Conservation of Angular Momentum under a central gravitational force
The inverse-square nature of gravitational force

explanation: Gravitational force is directed along the line joining planet to Sun (central force), producing zero net torque (τ = r × F = 0), so angular momentum is conserved.

title: Kepler's Third Law states that the square of the orbital period T of a planet is proportional to:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: The cube of the semi-major axis of its elliptical orbit (T² ∝ a³)
The square of the semi-major axis (T² ∝ a²)
The inverse cube of the semi-major axis

explanation: Kepler's harmonic law states T² = (4π² / GM) * a³, showing that planets farther from the Sun have disproportionately longer orbital years.

title: A geostationary communications satellite orbits Earth directly above the equator with an orbital period of:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: A geostationary satellite matches Earth's rotational period (23h 56m 4s), appearing stationary relative to ground tracking antennas.

title: Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation states that the gravitational attraction between two point masses m1 and m2 separated by distance r is:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Gravitation is a universal mutual attractive force proportional to mass product and inversely proportional to distance squared.

title: What is the numerical value of the Universal Gravitational Constant G, first measured by Henry Cavendish in 1798?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Cavendish measured G using a torsion balance, finding G ≈ 6.674 × 10^-11 N·m²/kg².

title: How does the acceleration due to gravity g vary with depth d beneath the surface of a uniform Earth of radius R?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: g(d) is constant all the way to the core

explanation: By Gauss's theorem for gravity, only mass within sphere of radius (R - d) attracts, so g decreases linearly to zero at Earth's center.

title: Bernoulli's Principle in fluid dynamics states that along a streamline in an ideal fluid:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: P + (1/2) * ρ * v² + ρ * g * h = constant

explanation: Bernoulli's equation expresses energy conservation for flowing fluids: high flow speed v corresponds to lower static pressure P.

title: The Equation of Continuity for an incompressible fluid flowing through a pipe of varying cross-sectional area states:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Conservation of mass in steady incompressible flow dictates that volumetric flow rate Q = A * v remains constant throughout the conduit.

title: Torricelli's Law states that the efflux speed v of an ideal liquid discharging through a small hole at depth h beneath a free surface is:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Applying Bernoulli's principle between the free surface and the orifice yields v = √(2gh), identical to the speed of free-fall from height h.

title: What is the terminal velocity of a small spherical ball of radius r and density ρ falling through a viscous fluid of viscosity η and density σ?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Equating gravitational net downward force (mg - buoyant force) to Stokes' drag force 6πηr v_t yields terminal velocity v_t = (2/9) r² g (ρ - σ) / η.

title: Reynolds number (Re) in fluid mechanics is a dimensionless ratio that characterizes the relative importance of:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Inertial forces to viscous forces in fluid flow
Gravitational forces to surface tension forces

explanation: Re = (ρ * v * L) / μ: low Re indicates smooth laminar flow dominated by viscosity, while high Re (> 4000) indicates turbulent flow.
