title: Snell's Law of Refraction relates the angles of incidence (θ1) and refraction (θ2) at a planar dielectric boundary by:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: n1 * sin θ1 = n2 * sin θ2
n1 * cos θ1 = n2 * cos θ2
n1 / sin θ1 = n2 / sin θ2
n1 * tan θ1 = n2 * tan θ2

explanation: Snell's Law states that the product of refractive index and sine of angle of propagation is conserved across planar interfaces.

title: Total Internal Reflection (TIR) can occur only when light travels from:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: An optically denser medium to an optically rarer medium at an angle exceeding the critical angle
A rarer medium to a denser medium at any angle
Vacuum into dense glass at 0° incidence

explanation: TIR requires light to propagate from a higher refractive index medium to lower (n1 > n2) at an angle of incidence θ1 > θ_c = arcsin(n2/n1).

title: What is the critical angle θc for total internal reflection at an interface between water (n = 1.33) and air (n = 1.00)?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Critical angle θc = arcsin(1.00 / 1.33) = arcsin(0.752) ≈ 48.8°.

title: The focal length f of a thin spherical lens with refractive index n and radii of curvature R1 and R2 in air is given by the Lens Maker's Formula:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The Lens Maker's Formula calculates thin lens focal power based on material refractive index and surface curvatures.

title: A convex lens of focal length f = +20 cm produces a real, inverted image at distance v = +30 cm. Where is the object located (using thin lens formula 1/f = 1/v - 1/u)?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: -60 cm (60 cm in front of lens)

title: What is the optical power in diopters (D) of a corrective converging lens with a focal length of +25 cm (+0.25 m)?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Optical power P in diopters is P = 1 / f(in meters) = 1 / 0.25 m = +4.0 D.

title: Young's Double-Slit Experiment definitively demonstrated which fundamental wave nature of light?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Thomas Young's 1801 experiment produced alternating bright and dark fringe bands, conclusively proving light behaves as an interfering wave.

title: In Young's Double-Slit Experiment with slit separation d, screen distance D, and light wavelength λ, the fringe width β is given by:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Fringe separation between consecutive bright bands is β = λD/d, proportional to wavelength and screen distance.

title: Brewster's Law states that reflected light is completely plane-polarized when the angle of incidence θp satisfies:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: At Brewster's angle, reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular (90° apart), completely eliminating s-polarized reflection.

title: Diffraction of light through a narrow single slit of width 'a' produces a central maximum whose angular half-width is given by:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The first diffraction minimum occurs when path difference between edges is λ, giving a * sin θ = λ or sin θ = λ/a.

title: Rayleigh's Criterion for the limit of resolution of an optical instrument (such as a telescope objective of diameter D) states that two point sources are barely resolved when angular separation θ is:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Rayleigh's criterion requires the central maximum of one Airy disk to fall on the first diffraction minimum of the other: θ = 1.22 λ/D.

title: Chromatic aberration in optical lenses, where different colors focus at different points, occurs because:
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: The refractive index of glass varies with wavelength (dispersion)
Lens curvature varies with atmospheric humidity
Light undergoes diffraction at the lens aperture

explanation: Dispersion causes blue light (shorter wavelength) to refract more strongly than red light, focusing closer to the lens.

title: Which optical device is completely free of chromatic aberration because it uses reflection rather than refraction to focus light?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The law of reflection (angle of incidence = angle of reflection) is independent of light wavelength, eliminating chromatic aberration in mirrors.

title: A magnifying glass (simple microscope) of focal length f produces a maximum angular magnification for a normal eye (near point D = 25 cm) equal to:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: When the image is formed at the near point D = 25 cm, angular magnification is M = 1 + D/f. When at infinity, M = D/f.

title: In a compound microscope, the intermediate image formed by the objective lens before magnification by the eyepiece is:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: The objective lens forms a real, inverted, magnified image just inside the focal point of the eyepiece.

title: The phenomenon responsible for the brilliant iridescent colors seen on thin soap bubbles and oil slicks on wet pavement is:
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Light waves reflecting from the upper and lower surfaces of a thin dielectric film interfere constructively or destructively depending on film thickness and wavelength.

title: Why is the daytime clear sky blue, as explained by Lord Rayleigh's scattering theory?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Shorter blue wavelengths scatter much more intensely than red wavelengths (I ∝ 1/λ^4)
Atmospheric oxygen molecules absorb red light preferentially
Sunlight loses blue frequencies in the upper stratosphere
Water vapor selectively emits blue photons

explanation: Rayleigh scattering by molecules much smaller than light wavelength scales inversely with the fourth power of wavelength (1/λ^4), scattering blue light 10 times more than red light.

title: Why do sunrises and sunsets appear vividly orange and red?
subject: Physical Sciences

options.text: Sunlight traverses a much thicker atmospheric path, scattering away blue wavelengths and leaving transmitted red light
Solar surface temperature drops at dusk and dawn
Atmospheric dust absorbs red light preferentially
Refraction turns all visible light red at 0° elevation

explanation: At low sun angles, sunlight passes through up to 10 times more air mass, completely scattering out blue and violet light before reaching the observer.

title: What is the speed of light in a glass prism having an optical refractive index of n = 1.50 (given c = 3.00 × 10^8 m/s in vacuum)?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Refractive index is n = c / v, so speed in glass is v = c / n = (3.00 × 10^8 m/s) / 1.50 = 2.00 × 10^8 m/s.

title: When a light wave crosses from air into a glass block, which characteristic of the wave remains completely unchanged?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Wave frequency is determined by the oscillation rate of the source and remains invariant across all media boundaries, while v and λ change (v = f * λ).

title: What is the optical power in diopters (D = 1/f) of a thin converging convex lens with focal length f = +30 cm?
subject: Physical Sciences
explanation: Optical power P in diopters is P = 1 / f(in meters). For f = +30 cm = +0.3 m, P = 1 / 0.3 = +3.33 D.

explanation: Optical power P in diopters is P = 1 / f(in meters). For f = +100 cm = +1 m, P = 1 / 1 = +1.00 D.

title: In a right-angled triangle, if the two legs have lengths 6 cm and 8 cm, what is the length of the hypotenuse?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: By the Pythagorean Theorem, c = √(a² + b²) = √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 cm.

title: What is the fundamental trigonometric Pythagorean identity connecting sine and cosine for any real angle θ?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: sin² θ + cos² θ = 1 is the fundamental trigonometric identity derived directly from the unit circle equation x² + y² = 1.

title: What is the exact value of tan(45°) in trigonometry?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: For a 45°-45°-90° right triangle, the opposite and adjacent legs are equal, so tan(45°) = opposite / adjacent = 1.

title: What is the exact value of sin(30°)?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: In a 30°-60°-90° right triangle, the side opposite the 30° angle is half the hypotenuse, so sin(30°) = 1/2.

title: What is the exact value of cos(60°)?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: By complementary angle identity, cos(60°) = sin(90° - 60°) = sin(30°) = 1/2.

title: The Law of Cosines for any arbitrary triangle with side lengths a, b, c and included angle C opposite side c is:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative

options.text: c = a * cos B + b * cos A

explanation: The Law of Cosines c² = a² + b² - 2ab cos C generalizes the Pythagorean Theorem to non-right triangles.

title: The Law of Sines states that for any triangle with angles A, B, C and opposite sides a, b, c:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative

options.text: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C = 2R
a * sin A = b * sin B
a / cos A = b / cos B
sin A + sin B = sin C

explanation: The Law of Sines relates side lengths to the sines of opposite angles, equaling the diameter 2R of the circumscribed circle.

title: What is the formula for the double angle identity of sine: sin(2θ)?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: Using the angle addition formula sin(θ + θ) = sin θ cos θ + cos θ sin θ = 2 sin θ cos θ.

title: Which of the following is an expression for the double angle formula of cosine: cos(2θ)?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: cos(2θ) = cos² θ - sin² θ = 2 cos² θ - 1 = 1 - 2 sin² θ.

title: In Euclidean geometry, the sum of the interior angles of any triangle is strictly equal to:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: In flat Euclidean plane geometry, interior angles of any triangle sum to 180° (or π radians).

title: What is the sum of the interior angles of an n-sided convex polygon in Euclidean geometry?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: Triangulating from one vertex divides an n-gon into (n - 2) non-overlapping triangles, giving interior angle sum (n - 2) * 180°.

title: What is the measure of each interior angle in a regular hexagon (6-sided regular polygon)?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: Sum of interior angles = (6 - 2) * 180° = 720°. Each angle = 720° / 6 = 120°.

title: What is the area of a circle with radius r?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: Area enclosed by a circle of radius r is A = π r².

title: What is the surface area of a sphere of radius r?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: Surface area of a sphere is 4π r², four times the area of its great equatorial disk.

title: What is the volume of a sphere of radius r?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: Volume of a solid sphere derived by Archimedes is V = (4/3) π r³.

title: The Inscribed Angle Theorem states that an angle inscribed in a circle is:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative

options.text: Half the measure of the central angle that subtends the same arc

explanation: An inscribed angle is exactly half the intercepted central arc angle (θ_inscribed = (1/2) θ_central).

title: Thales's Theorem states that any angle inscribed in a semicircle is strictly:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: Any triangle inscribed in a circle with the diameter as hypotenuse forms a 90° right angle at the circumference.

title: In coordinate geometry, the distance d between two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) in the Cartesian plane is:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: Direct application of the Pythagorean Theorem on Cartesian grid coordinates yields the Euclidean distance formula.

title: Two non-vertical lines in the Cartesian plane with slopes m1 and m2 are perpendicular if and only if:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: Perpendicular lines have negative reciprocal slopes: m2 = -1 / m1, meaning m1 * m2 = -1.

subject: Mathematics & Quantitative

title: A square matrix A is called invertible (non-singular) if and only if its determinant is:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: A square matrix has a multiplicative inverse A^-1 if and only if det(A) ≠ 0.

title: The trace of an n x n square matrix is defined as:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative

options.text: The sum of the elements along the main diagonal
The product of all non-zero entries
The sum of all row determinants

explanation: Trace tr(A) = ∑ a_ii is the sum of main diagonal entries, and equals the sum of its eigenvalues.

title: For any two square n x n matrices A and B, the determinant of their matrix product det(A * B) equals:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative

title: A non-zero vector v is an eigenvector of a square matrix A corresponding to eigenvalue λ if:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: By definition, matrix transformation A acting on an eigenvector v merely scales it by eigenvalue factor λ without changing its span direction.

title: The characteristic equation used to determine the eigenvalues λ of an n x n matrix A is:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: Eigenvalues satisfy (A - λI)v = 0 for non-trivial v ≠ 0, requiring the characteristic polynomial det(A - λI) = 0.

subject: Mathematics & Quantitative

title: A real square matrix Q is called orthogonal if its transpose equals its inverse, satisfying:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: An orthogonal matrix preserves vector lengths and angles (Euclidean isometry) and has det(Q) = ±1.

title: What is the determinant of any real orthogonal matrix Q?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: det(Q^T Q) = det(I) = 1 => (det Q)² = 1 => det Q = ±1.

title: A symmetric real matrix A (satisfying A^T = A) always possesses which fundamental spectral property?

explanation: The Spectral Theorem guarantees that any real symmetric matrix has all real eigenvalues and an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors.

title: What is the derivative of f(x) = x^n with respect to x according to the Power Rule?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: By the power rule of differential calculus, d/dx(x^n) = n * x^(n - 1).

title: What is the derivative of f(x) = sin(x) with respect to x?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: d/dx(sin x) = cos x.

title: What is the derivative of f(x) = cos(x) with respect to x?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: d/dx(cos x) = -sin x.

title: What is the derivative of the natural exponential function f(x) = e^x?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: The natural exponential function is its own derivative: d/dx(e^x) = e^x.

title: What is the derivative of the natural logarithm f(x) = ln(x) for x > 0?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: d/dx(ln x) = 1/x for all x > 0.

title: L'Hôpital's Rule allows evaluating limits of indeterminate forms like [0/0] or [∞/∞] by taking:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative

options.text: The limit of the ratio of derivatives: lim [f'(x) / g'(x)]
The product of limits lim f(x) * lim g(x)

explanation: L'Hopital's rule states that if lim f(x)/g(x) is indeterminate, lim [f(x)/g(x)] = lim [f'(x)/g'(x)] provided the latter limit exists.

title: What is the fundamental limit: lim (x -> 0) [sin(x) / x] (where x is measured in radians)?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: By the Squeeze Theorem, cos x < (sin x)/x < 1 near 0, giving lim (x->0) [sin x / x] = 1.

title: The Product Rule for differentiating the product of two functions (u * v)' is:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: By the product rule, d/dx(uv) = u'v + uv'.

title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus connects differentiation and integration by asserting that if F'(x) = f(x), then ∫_a^b f(x) dx equals:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: The definite integral of f(x) over [a, b] is evaluated by subtracting the antiderivative values: F(b) - F(a).

title: What is the indefinite integral ∫ (1 / x) dx for x ≠ 0?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: The antiderivative of 1/x is the natural logarithm of the absolute value: ln|x| + C.

title: A standard, fair six-sided die is rolled once. What is the probability of rolling a prime number (2, 3, or 5)?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: There are 3 prime outcomes {2, 3, 5} out of 6 possible outcomes, so P = 3/6 = 1/2.

title: Bayes' Theorem expresses the conditional probability of an event A given that event B has occurred as:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: Bayes' Theorem updates prior probability P(A) using likelihood P(B|A) and evidence P(B) to compute posterior P(A|B).

title: What is the total area under the probability density curve of any valid continuous random variable across its entire domain?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative

title: The Central Limit Theorem (CLT) states that as sample size n becomes sufficiently large, the sampling distribution of the sample mean:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative

options.text: Approaches a normal distribution regardless of the underlying population shape
Collapses into a single discrete spike
Adopts the skewness of the raw population

explanation: The CLT proves that averages of independent random variables tend toward a Gaussian normal distribution as n increases (typically n ≥ 30).

title: In hypothesis testing, a Type I error occurs when:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative

options.text: A true null hypothesis is incorrectly rejected (False Positive)
A false null hypothesis fails to be rejected (False Negative)
The sample size is too small to calculate variance

explanation: Type I error probability is denoted by α (significance level), representing rejection of H0 when H0 is actually true.

title: In hypothesis testing, a Type II error occurs when:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative

options.text: A false null hypothesis fails to be rejected (False Negative)
A true null hypothesis is rejected
Degrees of freedom equal sample size

explanation: Type II error probability is denoted by β, representing failure to reject H0 when H1 is true (1 - β is statistical power).

title: What is the Greatest Common Divisor (GCD) of 48 and 18, computed via the Euclidean Algorithm?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: 48 = 18 * 2 + 12; 18 = 12 * 1 + 6; 12 = 6 * 2 + 0. The last non-zero remainder is 6.

title: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic asserts that every integer greater than 1:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative

options.text: Can be factored uniquely into prime numbers, up to the order of factors
Can be written as the sum of three distinct squares
Has an infinite number of prime divisors

explanation: Unique prime factorization is the cornerstone of number theory: every integer > 1 is uniquely factored into primes.

title: Fermat's Little Theorem states that if p is a prime number and a is an integer not divisible by p, then:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: Fermat's Little Theorem a^(p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p) is the foundation of RSA modular exponentiation and primality testing.

title: What is the value of 17 modulo 5 (17 mod 5)?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: 17 = 5 * 3 + 2, so the remainder is 2.

title: Euler's Totient function φ(n) counts the number of positive integers up to n that are relatively prime to n. For a prime p, φ(p) equals:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: Since every positive integer less than prime p shares no factors with p, φ(p) = p - 1.

title: In graph theory, an Eulerian circuit (a closed trail visiting every edge exactly once) exists in a connected graph if and only if:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative

options.text: Every vertex has an even degree

explanation: Euler proved that a connected graph has an Eulerian circuit if and only if all vertices have an even degree.

title: A tree in graph theory is defined as a connected undirected graph that:
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative

options.text: Is complete with all possible edges

explanation: A tree is an undirected graph that is connected and acyclic, having exactly (V - 1) edges for V vertices.

subject: Mathematics & Quantitative

At least one container must remain empty

explanation: If more pigeons than pigeonholes exist, at least one hole must harbor two or more pigeons.

title: What is the Boolean logic result of: NOT (A AND B) according to De Morgan's Law?
subject: Mathematics & Quantitative
explanation: De Morgan's law states that negation of a conjunction equals disjunction of negations: ¬(A ∧ B) = (¬A) ∨ (¬B).

title: Which SQL clause is used to filter rows returned by a query based on a specific boolean condition?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: The WHERE clause filters rows before any groupings or aggregate functions are calculated.

title: What is the key difference between the WHERE clause and the HAVING clause in SQL?
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: WHERE filters individual rows before grouping; HAVING filters aggregated groups after GROUP BY
WHERE is used only with numeric data; HAVING is used only with text
WHERE can only be used in subqueries; HAVING is used in the main query
There is no difference; they are interchangeable synonyms

explanation: The WHERE clause applies filters to raw record rows, whereas HAVING filters aggregate results produced by a GROUP BY clause.

title: Which SQL keyword is used to remove duplicate rows from the final query result set?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: SELECT DISTINCT column_name returns only unique, deduplicated values.

title: Which type of SQL JOIN returns all rows from the left table and matched rows from the right table, filling missing right-side values with NULL?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: A LEFT OUTER JOIN preserves all records from the left relation, returning NULL for right-relation columns when no match exists.

title: Which SQL aggregate function computes the arithmetic mean of a column containing numeric values?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: The AVG() aggregate function computes the numerical average of all non-null values in the specified column.

title: In relational database design, what is a Primary Key?
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: A candidate key column (or set of columns) that uniquely identifies each row in a table and cannot contain NULL values
A key that references a column in an external table
An index that speeds up full-text document searches
A temporary key assigned during an active transaction

explanation: A Primary Key uniquely identifies every tuple in a relation and strictly enforces entity integrity (no duplicate or null values).

title: What is the purpose of a Foreign Key constraint in relational databases?
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: To enforce referential integrity between two related tables
To automatically encrypt sensitive credit card numbers
To prevent a table from exceeding 1 gigabyte in size
To force columns to store binary data only

explanation: A Foreign Key ensures referential integrity by establishing that values in the child table must match a valid primary key in the referenced parent table.

title: In database transaction management, what does the 'A' in the ACID acronym stand for?
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: Atomicity (all operations within a transaction succeed, or the entire transaction is rolled back)

explanation: Atomicity ensures all-or-nothing execution: if any statement fails, the entire transaction is aborted and rolled back to its previous state.

title: In ACID transaction properties, what does 'Consistency' ensure?
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: The database transitions strictly from one valid state to another valid state, preserving all integrity constraints
All queries complete in less than 10 milliseconds
Data is replicated across at least three geographical continents
The same query always returns identical row counts

explanation: Consistency guarantees that database transactions preserve all schema rules, check constraints, cascades, and triggers.

title: In ACID transaction properties, what does 'Isolation' ensure?
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: Concurrent transactions execute without interfering with each other, producing results equivalent to sequential execution
The database operates on an isolated offline server
Tables cannot be joined across different schemas
Indexes are stored in separate memory partitions

explanation: Isolation ensures that intermediate uncommitted states of concurrent transactions remain invisible to each other according to the isolation level.

title: In ACID transaction properties, what does 'Durability' ensure?
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: Once a transaction is committed, its changes survive permanently even in the event of a subsequent system crash or power outage
The database hardware operates without maintenance for 10 years
Tables can store an infinite number of rows
Network latency is kept below 1 ms

explanation: Durability guarantees that committed data is safely persisted to non-volatile storage (via write-ahead logging WAL or disk sync).

title: Which transaction isolation level provides the highest level of data consistency, preventing dirty reads, non-repeatable reads, and phantom reads?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: Serializable is the strictest ANSI/ISO SQL isolation level, executing transactions as if they were executed in a strict serial order.

title: A 'Dirty Read' in database concurrency occurs when:
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: A transaction reads data that has been modified by another concurrent transaction that has not yet committed
A transaction re-reads a row and finds the values changed by a committed transaction
A query retrieves deleted records from the recycle bin
A table scan encounters corrupted disk sectors

explanation: A dirty read occurs under 'Read Uncommitted' when Transaction A reads modifications made by Transaction B before B commits or rolls back.

title: First Normal Form (1NF) in database normalization requires that:
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: All column attributes contain atomic (indivisible) values, and there are no repeating groups
All non-key attributes are fully functionally dependent on the entire primary key
There are no transitive dependencies between non-key attributes
Every determinant is a candidate key

explanation: 1NF eliminates multi-valued attributes and composite repeating groups, ensuring each table cell holds a single atomic value.

title: Second Normal Form (2NF) requires a relation to be in 1NF and additionally eliminate:
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: Partial dependencies (no non-prime attribute may depend on a proper subset of a composite primary key)

explanation: 2NF prevents partial functional dependencies on composite primary keys: every non-key column must depend on the whole key.

title: Third Normal Form (3NF) requires a relation to be in 2NF and additionally eliminate:
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: Transitive dependencies (no non-prime attribute may depend on another non-prime attribute)

explanation: 3NF requires that every non-key attribute must depend directly on the primary key, and nothing but the key ('the key, the whole key, and nothing but the key').

title: Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) is a stricter version of 3NF which requires that for every functional dependency X -> Y:
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: Y must be a prime attribute
X and Y must belong to the same composite key
Y must not contain NULL values

explanation: BCNF requires that every determinant X in non-trivial dependencies X -> Y must be a candidate key (superkey).

title: Which balanced tree data structure is most widely implemented as the default index structure in relational databases like PostgreSQL and MySQL InnoDB?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: B+ Trees store all actual records/pointers in leaf nodes linked sequentially, optimizing disk block I/O and range scans (BETWEEN, <, >).

title: What is the fundamental difference between a Clustered Index and a Non-Clustered Index?
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: A Clustered Index dictates the physical on-disk storage order of table rows (only one per table); Non-Clustered indexes are separate lookup structures
Clustered indexes can only be built on integer columns; Non-clustered on text only
Non-clustered indexes rewrite the table physically every time a row is inserted

explanation: Because table rows can only be sorted physically in one order on disk, a table can have only one clustered index (typically on the Primary Key).

title: The CAP Theorem for distributed data stores states that it is impossible for a distributed system to simultaneously provide more than two of which three guarantees?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: Eric Brewer's CAP Theorem proves that under network partition (P), a distributed system must trade off Consistency (C) vs Availability (A).

title: In SQL, which query correctly selects all records from the 'products' table where 'price' is strictly greater than 200?
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: GET ALL FROM products HAVING price > 200;
FIND IN products WHERE price IS 200;

explanation: The standard SQL syntax for row filtering uses SELECT * FROM table WHERE condition; hence SELECT * FROM products WHERE price > 200; is correct.

title: The CIA Triad constitutes the foundational model of information security, representing which three core principles?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: Confidentiality (preventing unauthorized access), Integrity (preventing unauthorized modification), and Availability (ensuring authorized access) form the CIA Triad.

title: What is the fundamental difference between Symmetric and Asymmetric cryptography?
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: Symmetric uses the same secret key for encryption and decryption; Asymmetric uses a public-private key pair
Symmetric is only used for hashing; Asymmetric is used for encryption
Asymmetric uses 8-bit keys; Symmetric uses 2048-bit keys

explanation: Symmetric algorithms (like AES) share a single secret key; asymmetric algorithms (like RSA) utilize mathematically linked public and private key pairs.

title: Which symmetric block cipher algorithm was selected by NIST in 2001 to replace DES as the official global encryption standard?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: AES (Rijndael cipher) supports key sizes of 128, 192, and 256 bits operating on 128-bit blocks, serving as the worldwide gold standard for symmetric encryption.

title: The RSA public-key cryptosystem relies for its mathematical security on the computational hardness of which mathematical problem?
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: Factoring large composite integers into their prime factors
Solving the discrete logarithm problem over elliptic curves
Finding shortest vectors in high-dimensional lattices
Computing discrete Fourier transforms in polynomial time

explanation: RSA's security is rooted in the fact that while multiplying two large prime numbers p and q is easy, factoring their product n = p*q is computationally intractable.

title: The Diffie-Hellman protocol allows two communicating parties to establish a shared secret over an insecure channel based on the difficulty of:
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: The Discrete Logarithm Problem in a finite cyclic group

explanation: Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange (1976) enables two parties to securely compute a common symmetric key without ever transmitting the secret key over the wire.

title: A cryptographic hash function (such as SHA-256) is designed to satisfy 'Collision Resistance', which means:
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: It is computationally infeasible to find two distinct inputs x and y such that hash(x) = hash(y)
The hash output can be easily decrypted back to the original message
The output length varies dynamically with the input message length
The hash function produces zero when given a blank input

explanation: Collision resistance guarantees that an attacker cannot find two different documents yielding the same cryptographic digest fingerprint.

title: Which widespread web application vulnerability occurs when malicious scripts are injected into trusted websites and executed in the browser of other users?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: XSS allows attackers to execute arbitrary JavaScript in victim browsers, stealing session cookies, auth tokens, or redirecting to phishing portals.

title: SQL Injection (SQLi) attacks occur primarily due to which programming flaw in web backends?
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: Concatenating unvalidated or unescaped user input directly into dynamic SQL queries
Using HTTPS instead of plain HTTP
Running databases on non-standard network ports
Exceeding the maximum RAM allocated to database buffers

explanation: SQLi occurs when user input is treated as executable SQL code. It is mitigated by using parameterized prepared statements and ORM abstractions.

title: Which security architecture principle dictates that users, processes, and systems should be granted only the minimum permissions necessary to complete their job?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: Least Privilege minimizes the attack surface and lateral movement: if an account or service is compromised, damage is strictly confined.

title: Zero Trust security architecture operates fundamentally on which central maxim?
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: 'Never Trust, Always Verify' (assume breach and authenticate every request)
'Trust Internal Network Users, Block External Packets'

explanation: Zero Trust eliminates implicit trust based on network location, verifying identity, device health, and context for every single access request.

title: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) requires presenting at least two different authentication categories, traditionally defined as:
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: Something you know (password), Something you have (phone/token), and Something you are (biometrics)
Two different passwords from two different emails
A password typed twice on two different keyboards
A username in uppercase and lowercase

explanation: True MFA requires evidence across distinct independent factors: knowledge (password/PIN), possession (hardware key/authenticator app), and inherence (fingerprint/face).

title: What is a 'Man-in-the-Middle' (MitM) network attack?
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: An attacker secretly intercepts, relays, and possibly alters communications between two parties who believe they are communicating directly
An attacker overloads a web server with 10 million ping packets
An attacker physically steals a laptop from an office desk
An attacker brute-forces an admin password using a dictionary file

explanation: In MitM attacks, the adversary eavesdrops or tampers with communications, mitigated by end-to-end encryption with mutual certificate validation.

title: Which network protocol secures World Wide Web traffic by encrypting HTTP communications with Transport Layer Security (TLS)?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: HTTPS encapsulates HTTP over TLS, providing bidirectional encryption, server authentication via digital certificates, and message integrity.

title: What type of malware encrypts a victim's files and documents, demanding payment in cryptocurrency in exchange for the decryption key?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: Ransomware (such as WannaCry or LockBit) holds organizational data hostage by encrypting file systems with asymmetric/symmetric hybrid cryptography.

title: Phishing is a social engineering attack that primarily relies on:
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: Deceptive fraudulent emails, websites, or messages designed to trick victims into revealing credentials or sensitive data
Scanning open firewall ports for buffer overflow vulnerabilities
Intercepting Wi-Fi packets using directional radio antennas
Deploying electromagnetic EMP devices against server racks

explanation: Phishing exploits human trust, masquerading as legitimate entities (banks, IT departments, executive leadership) to compromise credentials.

title: In RESTful web API design, which HTTP method is standardized to retrieve data from a server without producing side effects (idempotent and safe)?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: HTTP GET retrieves resource representations safely without modifying server state.

title: What HTTP response status code indicates that a requested web resource was successfully processed (Standard OK)?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: 200 OK is the standard HTTP status code for successful HTTP requests.

title: What HTTP response status code signifies that the requested resource could not be found on the server?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: 404 Not Found indicates that the server cannot locate the requested URI resource.

title: Which cloud computing service model delivers virtualized compute infrastructure (VMs, storage, virtual networks) where users manage the OS and runtime?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: IaaS (e.g., AWS EC2, Google Compute Engine) provides raw virtualized hardware infrastructure.

title: Which cloud computing model abstracts the underlying operating system and middleware, allowing developers to deploy application code without managing servers?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: PaaS (e.g., Heroku, AWS Elastic Beanstalk) manages OS, patching, and hardware, providing a turnkey application runtime.

title: What open-source container virtualization technology packages application code and all its dependencies into lightweight, portable, isolated user-space containers?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: Docker containerizes applications sharing the host OS kernel, offering instant startup and consistent dev-to-prod execution.

title: Kubernetes (K8s) is an open-source orchestration system primarily designed to automate the deployment, scaling, and management of:
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: Containerized applications across clusters of host machines
Domain Name System (DNS) registrar zone records

explanation: Originally developed by Google, Kubernetes automates container lifecycle management, self-healing, rolling updates, and service discovery.

title: Which client-side storage mechanism in web browsers allows storing key-value pairs with no expiration time across browser sessions?
subject: Computer Science & AI
explanation: HTML5 Web Storage localStorage persists key-value string data with ~5MB quota until explicitly cleared by the user or script.

title: In modern web architectures, a Content Delivery Network (CDN) accelerates website performance by:
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: Caching static assets (images, CSS, JS) on geographically distributed edge servers close to end-users
Executing all server-side SQL queries inside the browser
Converting IPv4 addresses into IPv6 MAC hashes

explanation: CDNs (like Cloudflare, CloudFront) minimize latency by serving cached assets from regional Points of Presence (PoPs) nearest the user.

title: What is the role of a Reverse Proxy (such as Nginx or HAProxy) in web infrastructure?
subject: Computer Science & AI

options.text: Sitting in front of web servers to distribute incoming client traffic (load balancing), terminate SSL/TLS, and cache responses
Encrypting client hard drives against physical theft
Preventing users from visiting social media websites
Converting HTTP requests into raw Ethernet frames

explanation: A reverse proxy protects backend origin servers, performs load balancing, health checks, and SSL termination.

title: Identify the correct verb tense in the sentence: 'She had finished her assignment before the class started.'
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: 'Had finished' is the Past Perfect tense (had + past participle), indicating an action completed before another past event.

title: Choose the sentence that correctly uses the Present Perfect Continuous tense:
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: They have been playing tennis for two hours.
They were playing tennis for two hours.
They are playing tennis since two hours.

explanation: Present Perfect Continuous uses 'have/has been + verb-ing' to denote an action starting in the past and continuing into the present.

title: Which form completes the sentence correctly: 'Neither of the applicants _______ qualified for the senior position.'
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: 'Neither' is an indefinite pronoun that takes a singular verb ('is') when followed by an 'of' phrase.

title: Select the correct past participle form of the irregular verb 'freeze':
subject: English & Language Arts

title: Complete the sentence with the correct subjunctive mood verb: 'If I _______ you, I would accept the scholarship offer.'

title: Identify the transitive verb in the following sentence: 'The chef baked a delicious strawberry cake for the banquet.'

explanation: 'Baked' is a transitive verb because it transfers action directly to the object ('cake').

title: Choose the correct modal auxiliary verb expressing strong obligation or necessity: 'Citizens _______ follow traffic safety laws.'

title: Which phrasal verb means 'to cancel or abandon an event'?

title: Choose the sentence with correct subject-verb agreement:
subject: English & Language Arts

The committee have reached their decision without voting.

explanation: When a collective noun ('committee') acts as a single unified entity, it takes a singular verb ('has reached').

title: Convert the active sentence into the correct passive voice: 'The architect designed the innovative solar library.'
subject: English & Language Arts

The innovative solar library is designed by the architect.

The architect was designed by the library.

explanation: In simple past passive, the object becomes the subject with 'was/were + past participle' ('was designed').

title: Which type of sentence is formed by two independent clauses joined by a coordinating conjunction (FANBOYS)?
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: A compound sentence contains at least two independent clauses linked by a coordinating conjunction (For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So).

title: Identify the complex sentence among the following options:
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: Although it was raining heavily, the students continued their football practice.
The bell rang and the students entered the classroom.
The sun rose early this morning.
She ran fast, but she missed the morning train.

explanation: A complex sentence contains one independent clause joined with at least one dependent (subordinate) clause ('Although it was raining heavily').

title: What is a sentence fragment in English grammar?
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: An incomplete grammatical construction that lacks an independent subject, verb, or complete thought
A sentence containing more than three clauses
A sentence written in passive voice

explanation: A sentence fragment is an unattached dependent clause or phrase masquerading as a standalone sentence.

title: What grammatical error is present in: 'She loves reading science fiction novels, she visits the library every weekend.'?
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: A comma splice occurs when two independent clauses are joined with only a comma without a coordinating conjunction.

title: Identify the sentence with correct parallel grammatical structure:
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: She enjoys hiking, swimming, and reading mystery novels.
She enjoys hiking, to swim, and she reads books.
She likes to hike, swimming, and novels.
She enjoys hiking, swimming, and to read.

explanation: Parallel structure requires all coordinate elements in a series to share the same grammatical form (all gerunds: hiking, swimming, reading).

title: Identify the dangling modifier in the sentence: 'Walking through the forest, the ancient oak trees looked majestic.'
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: 'Walking through the forest' (implies the trees were walking)

explanation: A dangling modifier occurs when the introductory modifying participle phrase lacks a logical subject to modify in the main clause.

title: Which conditional sentence expresses a hypothetical unreal situation in the present or future?
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: Second Conditional ('If I had a million dollars, I would travel the world.')

explanation: The Second Conditional (If + simple past, would + base verb) describes imaginary or unlikely present/future conditions.

title: Which conditional sentence expresses regret about an impossible counterfactual condition in the past?
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: Third Conditional ('If we had taken the earlier train, we would not have been late.')

explanation: The Third Conditional (If + past perfect, would have + past participle) describes unreal past conditions and their past consequences.

title: Convert the direct quotation into indirect speech: The teacher said, 'The Earth revolves around the Sun.'
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: The teacher said that the Earth revolves around the Sun.
The teacher said that the Earth revolved around the Sun.
The teacher said the Earth had revolved around the Sun.
The teacher asked if the Earth revolves around the Sun.

explanation: Universal scientific truths and general physical facts remain in the simple present tense even when reported in indirect speech.

title: Identify the sentence that uses grammatical inversion correctly for dramatic emphasis:
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: Rarely have I witnessed such an extraordinary musical performance.
Rarely I have witnessed such an extraordinary performance.
Have rarely I witnessed such performance.

explanation: Negative and restrictive adverbs (rarely, seldom, scarcely, never) placed at the start of a sentence trigger subject-auxiliary inversion ('have I witnessed').

title: Classify the grammatical structure of the following sentence: 'The talented young artist painted a magnificent landscape.'
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: Contains only one independent clause with subject and predicate. Therefore, it is a Simple sentence.

title: Classify the grammatical structure of the following sentence: 'The bell rang, and the excited children rushed outside.'
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: Contains two independent clauses joined by coordinating conjunction 'and'. Therefore, it is a Compound sentence.

title: Classify the grammatical structure of the following sentence: 'Because she prepared diligently, Maya scored the highest grade.'
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: Contains a subordinate adverbial clause ('Because she prepared diligently') and an independent clause. Therefore, it is a Complex sentence.

title: Classify the grammatical structure of the following sentence: 'Although it was midnight, Arjun continued coding, and Priya reviewed the tests.'
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: Contains two independent clauses and at least one dependent clause. Therefore, it is a Compound-complex sentence.

explanation: Contains only one independent clause with subject and predicate. Therefore, it is a Simple sentence.

title: Classify the grammatical structure of the following sentence: 'The bell rang, and the excited children rushed outside.'
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: Contains two independent clauses joined by coordinating conjunction 'and'. Therefore, it is a Compound sentence.

title: Classify the grammatical structure of the following sentence: 'Because she prepared diligently, Maya scored the highest grade.'
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: Contains a subordinate adverbial clause ('Because she prepared diligently') and an independent clause. Therefore, it is a Complex sentence.

title: Classify the grammatical structure of the following sentence: 'Although it was midnight, Arjun continued coding, and Priya reviewed the tests.'
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: Contains two independent clauses and at least one dependent clause. Therefore, it is a Compound-complex sentence.

title: Classify the grammatical structure of the following sentence: 'The talented young artist painted a magnificent landscape.'
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: Contains only one independent clause with subject and predicate. Therefore, it is a Simple sentence.

title: What is the standard natural order of cumulative adjectives in English before a noun (OSASCOMP)?
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: Opinion, Size, Age, Shape, Color, Origin, Material, Purpose
Size, Opinion, Color, Origin, Age, Material

explanation: The Royal Order of Adjectives is: Opinion -> Size -> Age -> Shape -> Color -> Origin -> Material -> Purpose.

title: Identify the comparative and superlative degrees of the irregular adjective 'good':
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: 'Good' is an irregular adjective: positive 'good', comparative 'better', superlative 'best'.

title: Identify the comparative and superlative degrees of the irregular adjective 'bad':
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: 'Bad' is an irregular adjective: positive 'bad', comparative 'worse', superlative 'worst'.

title: Choose the correct sentence distinguishing the adverb 'well' from the adjective 'good':
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: She plays the grand piano very well.
She plays the grand piano very good.

explanation: 'Well' functions as an adverb modifying the verb 'plays'; 'good' is an adjective modifying nouns.

title: What type of adverb is 'frequently' in the sentence: 'The professor frequently visits the astronomical observatory.'?
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: 'Frequently' answers 'how often' the action takes place, making it an Adverb of Frequency.

title: Identify the adverb of manner in the sentence: 'The detective examined the crime scene meticulously.'
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: 'Meticulously' describes the manner in which the detective examined the scene (answering 'how?').

title: Choose the sentence that correctly uses the comparative degree to compare two items:
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: Mount Everest is higher than K2.
Mount Everest is the highest of the two peaks.
Mount Everest is more high than K2.

explanation: When comparing exactly two items, use the comparative degree ('higher'), reserving the superlative ('highest') for three or more.

title: Which of the following words ending in '-ly' is an adjective, NOT an adverb?
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: 'Friendly' is an adjective (noun 'friend' + -ly); the other three are adverbs derived from adjectives.

title: Identify the correct participle adjective completing the sentence: 'The lecture was so _______ that several students fell asleep.'
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: Present participle adjectives (-ing) describe the cause of a feeling ('boring lecture'); past participles (-ed) describe the person experiencing it ('bored students').

title: Select the sentence that contains an adverb of degree:
subject: English & Language Arts

explanation: 'Extremely' modifies the adjective 'cold', intensifying its degree (answering 'how much?').

title: What type of noun represents a concept, idea, emotion, or quality that cannot be experienced with the physical five senses?
subject: English & Language Arts

subject: English & Language Arts

subject: English & Language Arts

title: What is the primary function of a semicolon (;) in standard English punctuation?
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: To link two closely related independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction
To introduce a direct formal quotation or bulleted list
To indicate the omission of letters in a contraction
To separate a dependent introductory clause from the main subject

explanation: A semicolon connects two complete, grammatically independent thoughts that share a close thematic relation.

title: What punctuation mark is used to introduce a formal list, an explanation, or a concluding elaboration following an independent clause?
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: A colon follows an independent clause to introduce an amplification, explanation, or list.

title: What is the 'Oxford Comma' (serial comma)?
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: The optional comma placed immediately before the coordinating conjunction in a series of three or more items
The comma placed between city and country names
The comma placed inside quotation marks in British English
A comma used after an introductory prepositional phrase of one word

explanation: The Oxford comma clarifies meaning before 'and/or' in lists (e.g., 'apples, oranges, and bananas').

title: Choose the sentence that correctly uses the apostrophe for the contraction of 'it is':
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: It's a beautiful morning for a walk.
Its a beautiful morning for a walk.
Its' a beautiful morning for a walk.

explanation: 'It's' with an apostrophe is strictly the contraction of 'it is' or 'it has'; 'its' without an apostrophe is the possessive pronoun.

title: Choose the sentence that correctly uses the possessive pronoun 'its':
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: The robotic rover recharged its batteries in the sunlight.
The robotic rover recharged it's batteries in the sunlight.
The robotic rover recharged its' batteries in the sunlight.
The robotic rover recharged it is batteries.

explanation: 'Its' is the neutral singular possessive pronoun, functioning like 'his' or 'her' with no apostrophe.

title: Which punctuation mark is used to indicate a sudden abrupt break in thought or an emphatic parenthetical aside?
subject: English & Language Arts
explanation: An em-dash creates dramatic emphasis or sets off parenthetical information far more strikingly than parentheses or commas.

title: An En-dash (–) is primarily used in professional typography to indicate:
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: A span or range of numbers, dates, or time intervals (e.g., pages 45–52, 1914–1918)

explanation: The en-dash (shorter than an em-dash, longer than a hyphen) denotes inclusive spans and ranges.

title: According to standard English capitalization rules, which of the following words must always be capitalized?
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: Proper nouns, nationalities, languages, and calendar months
Common nouns referring to seasons (spring, summer)
Directional compass points indicating travel towards the south

explanation: Proper nouns, languages (English, French), nationalities, days of the week, and months are always capitalized.

title: Compass directions (north, south, east, west) should be capitalized ONLY when they:
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: Designate specific recognized geographic regions or cultural identities (e.g., 'the American West', 'the Global South')
Indicate simple travel direction ('walk east two blocks')

explanation: Capitalize directions when they refer to specific geopolitical or geographic regions, but lowercase them for simple compass directions.

title: What is the purpose of an ellipsis (...) in written text?
subject: English & Language Arts

options.text: To indicate the deliberate omission of words from a quoted passage, or a trailing pause in thought

explanation: An ellipsis (three spaced or unspaced periods) marks an omission in quoted material or a lingering hesitation.

title: In political science, what defines a 'Parliamentary System' of governance as practiced in India and the United Kingdom?
subject: History & Polity

options.text: The executive branch derives its democratic legitimacy from and is directly accountable to the legislature
The President is directly elected and completely independent of parliament
The judiciary directly appoints cabinet ministers
Military commanders hold veto power over legislative bills

explanation: In a parliamentary system, the executive (Prime Minister and Cabinet) is drawn from and held accountable to the legislature (Parliament).

title: What distinguishes a 'Federal System' from a 'Unitary System' of government?
subject: History & Polity

options.text: Constitutional division of legislative and taxation powers between a central government and regional/state governments
The existence of a written constitution without regional courts
A unicameral parliament with direct proportional voting
Rule by a hereditary monarch assisted by an appointed council

explanation: Federalism divides sovereign constitutional authority between the national central authority and federating states/provinces.

title: The political doctrine of 'Separation of Powers' into Legislative, Executive, and Judicial branches was famously articulated by which French philosopher?
subject: History & Polity

options.text: Baron de Montesquieu (in 'The Spirit of the Laws', 1748)

explanation: Montesquieu argued that dividing government into three independent branches prevents tyranny and guarantees political liberty.

title: Which organ of the United Nations is primarily responsible for the maintenance of international peace and security?
subject: History & Polity
explanation: Under the UN Charter, the 15-member Security Council holds primary authority for international peacekeeping and sanctions.

title: How many permanent members (P5) with veto power serve on the United Nations Security Council?
subject: History & Polity

options.text: Five (United States, United Kingdom, France, Russia, China)

explanation: The P5 nations hold permanent seats and individual veto powers over substantive resolutions under Article 27 of the UN Charter.

title: The concept of 'Sovereignty' in international law, establishing that states have exclusive legal authority over their domestic territory without external interference, traces to which 1648 treaty?
subject: History & Polity
explanation: The 1648 Peace of Westphalia ended the Thirty Years' War and established the modern international state system of sovereign equality.

title: In international relations theory, 'Realism' posits that the international system is primarily characterized by:
subject: History & Polity

options.text: Anarchy (lack of a central global authority), where states act as rational self-interested actors seeking power and survival
Universal global brotherhood fostered by legal treaties
Economic determinism driven solely by multinational tech corporations
Inequity caused by international postal agreements

explanation: Realism (represented by Thucydides, Machiavelli, Morgenthau, and Mearsheimer) views international relations as competitive struggles for power.

title: In international relations theory, 'Liberalism' (or Idealism) emphasizes the importance of:
subject: History & Polity

options.text: International institutions, democratic peace, rule of law, and economic interdependence to foster global cooperation
Maximizing military nuclear warheads for unilateral deterrence

explanation: Liberal IR theory emphasizes that international law, multilateral organizations (UN, WTO), and democratic governance facilitate durable peace.

title: Which electoral system allocates legislative seats to political parties in proportion to the total vote share received by each party?
subject: History & Polity
explanation: Proportional representation ensures that a party winning 30% of popular votes receives approximately 30% of parliamentary seats.

title: The principle of 'Judicial Review'—the power of constitutional courts to declare legislative laws or executive acts unconstitutional—was established in US jurisprudence by:
subject: History & Polity
explanation: Chief Justice John Marshall established the doctrine of judicial review in Marbury v. Madison, cementing the judiciary's check on legislative power.

title: In international relations, where is the principal headquarters of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (military defense alliance) located?
subject: History & Polity
explanation: The headquarters of NATO is located in Brussels, Belgium.

title: Which periodic trend describes the energy released when an electron is added to an isolated neutral gaseous atom?
subject: Chemical Sciences
explanation: Electron affinity is the energy change accompanying addition of an electron to a neutral atom in the gaseous phase.

title: What is the most electronegative element on the Pauling scale, having a value of 3.98?
subject: Chemical Sciences
explanation: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity of any element due to its small atomic radius and high effective nuclear charge.

title: According to VSEPR theory, what is the geometric molecular shape of a methane molecule (CH4)?
subject: Chemical Sciences
explanation: Four bonding pairs with zero lone pairs adopt a regular tetrahedral geometry with 109.5° bond angles.

title: According to VSEPR theory, what is the geometric shape of a water molecule (H2O)?
subject: Chemical Sciences
explanation: Two bonding pairs and two lone pairs on oxygen compress the tetrahedral angle from 109.5° to approximately 104.5°.

title: What type of chemical bond is formed when one atom completely transfers one or more valence electrons to another atom?
subject: Chemical Sciences
explanation: An ionic bond arises from electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions formed by complete electron transfer.

title: What type of chemical bond involves the equal sharing of electron pairs between two atoms of similar electronegativity?
subject: Chemical Sciences
explanation: When electronegativity difference is minimal (ΔEN < 0.4), electron density is shared equally, forming a nonpolar covalent bond.

title: What is the hybridization of the central carbon atom in an ethylene molecule (C2H4, containing a C=C double bond)?
subject: Chemical Sciences
explanation: Carbon forms three σ bonds (trigonal planar) using sp² hybrid orbitals, with the unhybridized p orbital forming a π bond.

title: What is the hybridization of the carbon atoms in an acetylene molecule (C2H2, containing a C≡C triple bond)?
subject: Chemical Sciences
explanation: Each carbon forms two σ bonds using sp hybrid orbitals (linear 180°) and two perpendicular π bonds from unhybridized p orbitals.

title: According to Molecular Orbital (MO) Theory, why is diatomic oxygen (O2) paramagnetic in its ground state?
subject: Chemical Sciences

options.text: It contains two unpaired electrons in degenerate π* antibonding molecular orbitals
It has a complete octet with all electrons paired
It has zero net nuclear spin

explanation: MO theory explains that O2 fills π*2px and π*2py orbitals with one unpaired electron each, explaining its experimentally observed paramagnetism.

title: What is the bond order of diatomic nitrogen (N2) according to Molecular Orbital Theory?
subject: Chemical Sciences
explanation: Bond order = (N_bonding - N_antibonding) / 2 = (8 - 2) / 2 = 3.0, explaining nitrogen's exceptional chemical inertness.

title: Which hormone secreted by pancreatic alpha cells stimulates glycogenolysis in the liver to raise blood glucose during fasting?
subject: Life Sciences & Health
explanation: Glucagon acts antagonistically to insulin, stimulating glycogen breakdown in the liver to increase blood sugar.

title: Which endocrine gland is often referred to as the 'Master Gland' of the human body because its trophic hormones regulate other endocrine glands?
subject: Life Sciences & Health
explanation: The pituitary gland, located at the base of the brain under hypothalamic control, secretes hormones like TSH, ACTH, LH, and FSH.

title: Which class of immunoglobulins (antibodies) is the most abundant in human blood serum and can cross the placenta to provide passive immunity to the fetus?
subject: Life Sciences & Health
explanation: IgG accounts for ~75-80% of human antibodies and is the only antibody class capable of crossing the placental barrier.

title: Which immunoglobulin class is primarily present in human body secretions (saliva, tears, breast milk/colostrum) providing mucosal immunity?
subject: Life Sciences & Health
explanation: Secretory IgA protects mucosal surfaces of respiratory and gastrointestinal tracts from viral and bacterial entry.

title: Which white blood cells are primarily responsible for cell-mediated adaptive immunity by directly destroying virus-infected cells and tumor cells?
subject: Life Sciences & Health
explanation: Cytotoxic CD8+ T cells recognize foreign antigens presented on MHC Class I molecules and release perforins/granzymes to induce apoptosis.

title: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measured by the expenditure approach is calculated using which standard macroeconomic identity?
subject: General Awareness & Logic
explanation: GDP equals Consumer Spending (C) + Investment (I) + Government Purchases (G) + Net Exports (X - M).

title: What is the fundamental difference between Nominal GDP and Real GDP?
subject: General Awareness & Logic

options.text: Real GDP is adjusted for inflation using constant base-year prices; Nominal GDP is measured at current market prices
Real GDP includes exports; Nominal excludes imports
Nominal GDP is calculated by private banks; Real GDP by the UN

explanation: Real GDP eliminates the distortions of price inflation, measuring the actual volume of goods and services produced.

title: What economic phenomenon describes an economy experiencing stagnant economic growth, high unemployment, and high inflation simultaneously?
subject: General Awareness & Logic
explanation: Stagflation (stagnant growth + inflation) challenged traditional Phillips curve Keynesian economics during the 1970s oil crises.

title: What is the primary monetary policy interest rate at which a central bank (such as the RBI in India) lends short-term money to commercial banks against government securities?
subject: General Awareness & Logic
explanation: The Repo Rate is the key policy interest rate used by central banks to control liquidity, inflation, and credit creation.

title: The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) mandates that commercial banks must hold a specified minimum percentage of their net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) as:
subject: General Awareness & Logic

options.text: Cash deposits maintained directly with the Central Bank
Equity shares in public infrastructure corporations

explanation: CRR is an unremunerated cash reserve held with the central bank to ensure bank liquidity and control credit multiplier expansion.

title: What is the fractional reserve banking 'Money Multiplier' formula assuming a required reserve ratio of RR?
subject: General Awareness & Logic
explanation: In simple deposit expansion, maximum potential credit creation equals initial reserve deposit multiplied by (1 / RR).

title: In international economics, the classical Theory of Comparative Advantage, demonstrating that nations benefit from trade even if one country has an absolute advantage in all goods, was formulated by:
subject: General Awareness & Logic
explanation: David Ricardo proved that trade specialization based on lower opportunity cost maximizes total global output and consumer welfare.

title: A nation's Balance of Payments (BoP) consists of two main accounts:
subject: General Awareness & Logic
explanation: The Current Account tracks trade in goods/services and remittances; the Capital/Financial Account records cross-border investments and financial flows.

title: When a central bank increases interest rates to curb rising inflation, what is the typical expected effect on the domestic currency exchange rate?
subject: General Awareness & Logic

options.text: The domestic currency tends to appreciate due to higher foreign capital inflows seeking yields
The exchange rate freezes by statutory law
The domestic currency is replaced by gold

explanation: Higher relative interest rates attract foreign portfolio investment, raising demand for the domestic currency and leading to appreciation.

title: Which international financial institution headquartered in Washington D.C. was established at the 1944 Bretton Woods Conference to ensure international financial stability and assist member nations facing balance-of-payments crises?
subject: General Awareness & Logic
explanation: The IMF oversees the global monetary system and provides financial stabilization loans to countries experiencing severe currency or debt crises.

explanation: Money Multiplier = 1 / (RR/100) = 100 / 6 = 16.67.

subject: General Awareness & Logic
explanation: Money Multiplier = 1 / (RR/100) = 100 / 7 = 14.29.

title: In which atmospheric layer does virtually all of Earth's active weather (clouds, rain, storms) take place?
subject: Geography & Environment

options.text: Troposphere (extending from surface to ~12 km altitude)

explanation: The troposphere contains ~75% of atmospheric mass and 99% of total water vapor, driving all planetary weather systems.

title: The protective ozone layer, which absorbs harmful solar ultraviolet (UV-B and UV-C) radiation, is located primarily in which layer of the atmosphere?
subject: Geography & Environment
explanation: The stratospheric ozone layer prevents high-energy solar UV photons from reaching the surface, preventing DNA damage and cataracts.

title: What is the Coriolis effect, and how does it influence winds in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres?
subject: Geography & Environment

options.text: Earth's rotation deflects moving air masses to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere
Earth's magnetic field accelerates ionized air toward the equator
Solar radiation causes winds to blow strictly north-south
Lunar tidal pull forces clouds to rotate eastward

explanation: Due to Earth's counterclockwise rotation, objects moving across the surface experience an apparent Coriolis deflection (right in North, left in South).

title: What is the calm, low-pressure center of a mature tropical cyclone characterized by light winds and clear skies called?
subject: Geography & Environment
explanation: The eye is a roughly circular area of descending air and lightest winds at the cyclone's center, surrounded by the violent eyewall.

title: What natural climate phenomenon refers to the periodic warming of sea surface temperatures across the central and east-central equatorial Pacific Ocean?
subject: Geography & Environment
explanation: El Niño (part of ENSO) alters global atmospheric jet streams, often leading to drought in India and Australia and torrential rains in South America.

title: The Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ), known historically to sailors as the 'doldrums', is characterized by:
subject: Geography & Environment

options.text: A low-pressure belt near the equator where the northeast and southeast trade winds converge, producing intense convective thunderstorms
A high-pressure anticyclonic desert belt at 30° latitude

explanation: The ITCZ shifts seasonally north and south with solar declination, driving the monsoon rains across South Asia and Africa.

title: Which meteorological instrument is used to measure atmospheric pressure?
subject: Geography & Environment
explanation: Mercury and aneroid barometers measure atmospheric air pressure, crucial for forecasting storms and high-pressure fair weather.

title: Which meteorological instrument is specifically used to measure wind speed?
subject: Geography & Environment
explanation: An anemometer (typically rotating cups or ultrasonic sensors) measures wind velocity, while a wind vane indicates direction.

title: What is 'Relative Humidity' in meteorology?
subject: Geography & Environment

options.text: The ratio of the actual amount of water vapor in the air to the maximum amount the air can hold at that temperature, expressed as a percentage
The absolute mass of water vapor per cubic meter of air
The temperature at which rain begins to freeze
The pressure difference between troposphere and stratosphere

explanation: When relative humidity reaches 100%, the air is fully saturated at its dew point and condensation begins forming clouds or dew.

title: Which greenhouse gas has the largest overall contribution to Earth's natural greenhouse effect?
subject: Geography & Environment
explanation: Water vapor accounts for ~60% of Earth's natural greenhouse warming; human emissions of CO2 amplify water vapor feedback.

title: In meteorological cloud classification, what describes 'Cirrus' clouds?
subject: Geography & Environment

options.text: High-altitude, wispy, feathery ice-crystal clouds appearing above 6,000 meters
Dense volcanic ash clouds trapped in the mesosphere
Stratospheric radioactive clouds from cosmic rays

explanation: 'Cirrus' clouds are defined as: High-altitude, wispy, feathery ice-crystal clouds appearing above 6,000 meters.

title: In meteorological cloud classification, what describes 'Cumulonimbus' clouds?
subject: Geography & Environment

options.text: Towering vertical thunderstorm clouds capable of producing heavy rain, hail, and lightning
Dense volcanic ash clouds trapped in the mesosphere
Stratospheric radioactive clouds from cosmic rays

explanation: 'Cumulonimbus' clouds are defined as: Towering vertical thunderstorm clouds capable of producing heavy rain, hail, and lightning.

title: In meteorological cloud classification, what describes 'Stratus' clouds?
subject: Geography & Environment

options.text: Low, uniform, gray featureless cloud layer covering the sky like a fog blanket
Dense volcanic ash clouds trapped in the mesosphere
Stratospheric radioactive clouds from cosmic rays

explanation: 'Stratus' clouds are defined as: Low, uniform, gray featureless cloud layer covering the sky like a fog blanket.

title: In meteorological cloud classification, what describes 'Altocumulus' clouds?
subject: Geography & Environment

options.text: Mid-level patchy white or gray sheet clouds formed of water droplets
Dense volcanic ash clouds trapped in the mesosphere
Stratospheric radioactive clouds from cosmic rays

explanation: 'Altocumulus' clouds are defined as: Mid-level patchy white or gray sheet clouds formed of water droplets.

Dense volcanic ash clouds trapped in the mesosphere
Stratospheric radioactive clouds from cosmic rays

title: In meteorological cloud classification, what describes 'Cumulonimbus' clouds?
subject: Geography & Environment

options.text: Towering vertical thunderstorm clouds capable of producing heavy rain, hail, and lightning
Dense volcanic ash clouds trapped in the mesosphere
Stratospheric radioactive clouds from cosmic rays

explanation: 'Cumulonimbus' clouds are defined as: Towering vertical thunderstorm clouds capable of producing heavy rain, hail, and lightning.

title: In meteorological cloud classification, what describes 'Stratus' clouds?
subject: Geography & Environment

options.text: Low, uniform, gray featureless cloud layer covering the sky like a fog blanket
Dense volcanic ash clouds trapped in the mesosphere
Stratospheric radioactive clouds from cosmic rays

explanation: 'Stratus' clouds are defined as: Low, uniform, gray featureless cloud layer covering the sky like a fog blanket.

title: In meteorological cloud classification, what describes 'Altocumulus' clouds?
subject: Geography & Environment

options.text: Mid-level patchy white or gray sheet clouds formed of water droplets
Dense volcanic ash clouds trapped in the mesosphere
Stratospheric radioactive clouds from cosmic rays
